12287.details:
For time:
800m Run
-then-
20 Rounds of:
5 Hang Power Cleans
30 Double Unders
-then-
800m Run
12287.notes:
Party like it’s 2025!
Intent is 18-24 min.
Partners will run together. When both athletes are back in the gym, they’ll trade full rounds of work on the couplet. 20 total, 10 each person.
Hit the first run hard, but leave enough in the tank to get right to work on the middle portion of the workout. Attack the second run with everything you have left.
Barbell:
135/95/65#
On the light side of medium and unbroken throughout
+/- 60% of a max power clean is a good guideline
DU:
Scale reps so you spend no more than 30 sec here.
Modify to 30 sec of attempts or 50 Single Unders.
Run:
Scale to 550m if your mile pace is under 10 min.
Orthopedic substitute is 1600-2000m Bike (1-1.25 miles) each time.

12288.details:
3-5 Progressive Sets
A1. 5 Half Kneeling DB Press + 5 Half Kneeling DB Windmill, ea side
A2. 30 Sec L-Sit on Parallettes
12288.notes:
DB complex: Complete 5 presses and continue into 5 windmills. Rest as needed and repeat on second side. DB Press is ipsilateral: same side leg is forward as whichever arm is pressing.
L-Sit: Choose the hardest possible variation you can maintain position in for at least 10 seconds. You may accumulate time here, for example: 10 sec on / 10 sec off x 3 sets.
Scaling
A. 15 sec each side Single Leg Extended
B. 30 sec Tuck with alternating leg extensions
C. 30 sec Tuck
D. 30 sec Tuck on Matador

12288.details:
AMRAP 12 MIN
16 Alternating DB Power Snatches
16 Alternating DB Goblet Reverse Lunges
4 Wall Walks
12288.notes:
Intent is 5-7 rounds. Scale load, volume, or movement complexity as needed.
Snatches and lunges are 16 total alternating, 8 ea.
DB: +/50/35/20#/-
Choose 1 weight to use for both movements.
Wall Walks:
A. 2-3 Full Range of Motion
B. 4 Partial ROM
C. 2x (10 Sec Angled Wall Hold + 10 sec Rest)

12285.notes:
Use notes from Fri 10/11/24 if you were here!
You can go sets across or build today, depending on your experience with this variation and the time it takes you to warm up. Work towards RPE 8/10 or so.

12285.details:
For Max Calories
2:00 Row or Bike
2:00 Rest
2:00 Bike or Row
2:00 Rest
1:30 Row or Bike
1:30 Rest
1:30 Bike or Row
1:30 Rest
1:00 Row or Bike
1:00 Rest
1:00 Bike or Row
1:00 Rest
12285.notes:
This is a solo workout, but in large classes you’ll buddy up to share equipment with someone. Athlete A starts on the erg. Athlete B starts on the bike.
Each person works at the same time for a 2 minute interval. Then rest, switch equipment, and repeat on the second machine. Continue in this fashion for the following intervals.
Note your calories completed for each individual interval. This is your score.
Your goal is to find a tough pace from the beginning without redlining so you can work hard across all 6 intervals.
Part of what we’re training here is your ability to recover. Be intentional in your rest period:
-Keep your legs moving
-Slow your exhales down
-Close your mouth and nasal breathe as soon as possible
-Mentally commit to your next effort

12297.details:
AMRAP 7 Min
1-3-5-7-etc. Reps Each:
Thrusters @ 135/95/65#
Bar Muscle Ups
Rest 7 Min
AMRAP 7 Min
3-6-9-12-etc. Reps Each:
Front Squats @ 135/95/65#
Kipping Pull Ups
12297.notes:
Intent is to get through at least 4 rounds of each couplet. Scale accordingly to your current abilities.
The first section should challenge you in terms of gymnastic skill and load. The second section will be simpler… but not easy.
Barbell: Heavy weight you can do 3-5 thrusters with unbroken.
Gymnastics: Athletes may first choose a volume scale, for example:
1-2-3-4-etc. BMU
2-4-6-8, etc. Kipping Pull Ups.
When scaling further, choose a harder variation in the first section and an easier variation in the second section, relative to your skill and strength, for example:
A: Kipping Chest To Bar Pull Ups / Kipping Pull Ups
B. Strict CTB Pull Ups / Strict Pull Ups
C. Band Assisted Strict Pull Ups / Jumping Pull Ups

12298.notes: Start with a comfortable bag to work on your technique and then build a bit each set as appropriate. Don’t rush your reps, take time between each to get organized.

12298.details:
In 20:00 perform 3-5 sets of the following for load:
50′ Hip Bias Rope Pull
50′ Sled Push back
50′ Hip Bias Rope Pull
50′ Sled Push back
12298.notes:
Pull a sled with a 50′ Rope using a hip-biased technique. Push the sled back. Repeat and then rest. Aim to increase the load each set.
Option to bike for about 1 min easy recovery between your sets as you trade off with other athletes in class.

12301.details:
Every 5 min x 5 Rounds
10 Bench Press
15 KB Swings @ 24/16/12kg
Max Calorie Bike until 2:30 mark
12301.notes:
Intent is that the Bench and Swings are unbroken today, which should leave you with a good chunk of time to work hard on the bike! With equal rest today, each round should be tough effort.
BP: Ideally keep same weight across the rounds: 55-65% is a good guideline/starting point. If unsure, start conservatively and build.
KB: Moderate weight you can comfortably swing for 15 reps unbroken.

12305.details:
Part A.
8 Minutes to find a 1 Rep Max Squat Clean
Rest 10 Minutes
Part B.
8 Minute AMRAP Squat Cleans @ 90% of your best lift in Part A.
12305.notes:
After some barbell drills and a brief warm up period, you’ll take 8 minutes to find a heavy single on the squat clean. Use prior numbers and notes, to help you plan out your attempts. It won’t be a ton of time, so get your head right, commit to each lift, and see what you can do!
The second portion is tough. Your technique, efficiency, and ability to “recharge your battery” to create power and acceleration on the bar under fatigue will all have an impact here. The heart and lungs will be working, too!
If you tend to take a conservative approach, be bold today and see what it’s like to do the next lift before you feel completely “ready.” You may surprise yourself.

12306.details:
A1. DB Strict Press, 4 x 8-12
A2. Strict Chin Up, 4 x max reps (-1)
12306.notes:
Use a “slower-down, faster up” tempo on both movements.
Rest about 30 seconds after press, 60-90 seconds after chin ups.
DB Press: Start at moderate load and build. Aim to find a weight you physically cannot complete 12 reps with.
Chin Ups: Bodyweight. Leave 1 rep in reserve.
If you are not yet doing sets of 5+ reps unbroken, use the progression below to find a productive way to build strength today:
A. Bodyweight “Cluster Sets” (ex: 3+3 or 2+2+1, with 10-20 sec rest between)
B. Negatives, 4 x 2-3, as slow as possible
C. Box Pike or Banded, 4 x 4-6

12306.details:
3-5 Rounds for Quality and Load
5-10 Strict Toes to Bar
30 sec each side Contralateral Carry
Floater Movement (pick one)
Floater Options:
A. 10-15 Lying DB Tricep Extensions
B. 10 Good Mornings (DB/KB)
C. 600m Bike
D. 270m Run
12306.notes:
Aim to move steadily throughout your rounds.
If 10 Strict Unbroken TTB is no problem, scale up to “Around the Worlds.”

12312.details:
EMOM x 30 Min for Reps
A. 30 Sec Bike (cal)
B. 30 Sec Row (cal)
C. 30 Sec Double Unders
12312.notes:
Simple on paper, special in reality!
Start at 80-85% aerobic effort and note RPMs on the bike and Cal/Hr on the row you can hold. This will likely feel “too easy” for the first couple of rounds. Ride those paces through the first half, and if all is well, turn the dial up little by little on the back half.
Score = total number of reps completed in 30 min: calories on bike/row + number of DU’s.
Goal is to have a consistent output across 10 rounds (within 1-2 calories and within 5 or so DU’s), knowing that effort will increase as fatigue accumulates.
DU Scaling: 30 sec practice for at least 5 rounds, then you can opt for single unders!
If you have a goal to get more consistent double unders this year, today is a great day to start. Keep your paces a little easier on the row and bike for starters so you can devote good practice time to the rope.

12317.details:
A. Bench Press, 3×4-6
B. Back Squat, 3×6-8
C. Squat Clean, 1-1-1-1
D. Strict Press, 3×8-12
E. Deadlift, 3×6-8
12317.notes:
Tomorrow we have rowing, lunges, and burpees.
You may superset with a non-interfering bodyweight or DB/KB movement if desired.
The lifts can be sets across or building!
Option C: If you get to a max early in your lifting time, come back down to 80-85% and work some more reps there to refine technique.

12317.details:
4 Rounds for max reps of:
1:00 AMRAP Shuttle Runs
1:00 Rest
1:00 AMRAP Wall Ball Shots
1:00 Rest
12317.notes:
This is a repeat WOD. Track back to 4/19/24 and see if you can get more work accomplished today.
Run, Ball, rinse, repeat! Push hard on each interval.

12318.details:
For Time:
3000m Row
400′ DB Suitcase Walking Lunges (50/35/20# ea)
100 Burpees
12318.notes:
Intent: 20-28 min workout, with a 30 minute cap. Utilize your scaling options to finish your version of the workout under the cap!
You and a buddy will accumulate the total work listed as a team, chipper style, trading off as desired. Aim to split the work evenly. The entire row must be completed before moving on to the lunges, and again to the burpees.
Example method:
Partners trade 300m row segments, 5 intervals each.
Partners trade 40′ segments of lunging, 5 each.
Partners trade off quick sets of 5 burpees!
Lunges: 20′ segments across the gym. Start with toes behind the near line and finish with heels beyond the far line. Turn and repeat. It might be tempting to cut your last few inches short, but hold the standard on each segment.
Scaling Option A – scale weight as needed
2400m Row
320′ Lunges
80 Burpees
Scaling Option B- scale weight as needed
1800m Row
240′ Lunges
60 Burpees

12321.details:
A. Bench Press, 3×4-6
B. Back Squat, 3×6-8
C. Squat Clean, 1-1-1-1
D. Strict Press, 3×8-12
E. Deadlift, 3×6-8
12321.notes:
Tomorrow we have biking, kipping pull ups, box jump overs, and running.
You may superset with a non-interfering bodyweight or DB/KB movement if desired.
These lifts can be sets across or building.
Option C: If you get to a max early in your lifting time, come back down to 80-85% and work some more reps there to refine technique.

12321.details:
4 Rounds for Time:
20 Alternating DB Power Snatches
20 Tuck Ups
12321.notes:
Intent <9:00. Scale load or volume as needed.
DB: +/50/35/20#/-. Choose a challenging load you can do in 1-2 sets each round.
Tuck Ups: Gold standard is to start and finish in a hollow body position on each rep and to rise to the tailbone in the middle. Arms can stay reaching forward throughout, or reach overhead if you prefer it.
Scaling Option:
4 Rounds
16 Alt Snatches
16 Tuck Ups or Abmat Sit Ups

12325.details:
For Time:
50/40 Cal Bike
Rest 1 Min
5 Rounds of:
12 Kipping Pull Ups
8 Box Jump Overs (24/20/16″)
Rest 1 Min
800m Run
12325.notes:
Complete all of the work above on a running clock. Score is your total time to complete, including the rest.
Intent: 16-22 min, including rest.
Bike <5 min. Scale calories as needed.
Run <5 min. Scale to 670m. Orthopedic sub = 1000m Row.
Pull-Ups: Should be done in 1-2 sets per round. Full volume is appropriate if you have sets of 10+ reps unbroken.
Pull-up Scaling
RX+ Chest to Bar
A. 8-10 Kipping
B. 6 Strict
C. 6 Strict Box PIke or Band Assisted
Box Jump Overs:
Athletes do not need to come hip or leg extension at the top of the box.
Athletes must step down off the box. Rebounding is not allowed.
You may face the box or be parallel to it for a lateral jump.

12327.details:
Every 2 min x 8 Sets
2 Squat Snatches + 2 Overhead Squats
12327.notes:
The snatches are not touch and go. After your first rep, reset the bar to the floor and take at least 5 seconds to organize before the second rep.
Start at 50% of your best snatch. If you don’t know it, use about 70-80% of your best clean from last week as a substitute for a 1 RM.
*Example: 100# clean last week = assume 75# Snatch. Start at 35-40# today.
Newer lifters can work with moderate loads throughout to build mechanics and consistency on the lift.
Int + Adv lifters: Add ~5% to the bar each set, working up towards 85%. The numbers don’t have to be perfect, just ballpark. If you miss a lift, repeat or decrease load and wave up again.
*Example: 1 RM = 135#. Work Sets:
65, 75, 85, 95, 100, 105, 110, 115#
Track back to 12/4/24 (3×6-10) or 12/11/24 (Heavy 5) for some guidance on loading today. Leave1-2 reps in the tank on each set.

12331.details:
A1. Bench Press 3×4-6
A2. Three Point DB Row 3×8-12
12331.notes:
Take 2-4 warm up sets on the bench press before your work sets. These can be progressive, or go sets across if you’re confident of where to start. Track back to notes on three point DB rows and see if you can meet or beat some previous numbers.
Rest about 1 min between movements, more if needed.

12331.details:
AMRAP 16:00
16 Burpees
20 DB Deadlifts @ 50s/35s/20s
24 Abmat Sit Ups
12331.notes:
Intent ~5-7 Rounds
The burpees are a meaty portion of this workout. Use a scaling option that you can complete in about 1 min or less per round:
A. 12 full ROM
B. 8 full ROM + 8 no-push-up
C. 4 full ROM + 8 no-push-up
DL: 1-2 sets throughout. Only the front globe of the DB needs to touch the floor. Come to full hip and knee extension on each rep; these are easy to get sloppy on.
SU: Scale by squeezing a KB between your feet.

12333.details:
Every 4 min x 6 Intervals
15/12/9 Cal Row
10 Front Rack Reverse Lunges, 5ea
Max Reps Wall Walks to the 2:30 mark of each round
Rest 1:30
12333.notes:
Row < 1 min. Scale as needed to a number you can do with 80-85% aerobic effort in that timeframe consistently.
Lunges: +/115/80/55#/-. Unbroken, but challenging.
The goal is to get to the wall walks with at least 45 sec to work. Adjust as needed.
The wall is not necessarily a place to “die for points” today. Be measured in your first couple intervals until you get a feel for it, and then aim for consistency. Safety first!
WW Scaling
A. Full range of motion
B. Partial range of motion
C. Angled hollow body hold OR Box Pike Handstand Hold

12334.details:
A. Bench Press, 3×4-6
B. Back Squat, 3×6-8
C. (2 Squat Snatches + 2 Overhead Squats) x 6-8 Sets
D. Strict Press, 3×8-12
E. Deadlift, 3×6-8
12334.notes:
Tomorrow we have power clean & jerks and toes to bar.
The lifts can be sets across or building. Rep schemes are the same as last week for ABDE, so aim to increase reps in the range if you were at the low end OR increase load if you were maxing out the reps.
Snatch Complex: Beginner lifters should work with light to moderate load and aim for consistency in positions and range of motion. Int/Adv lifters: start at 50% and build by about 5% each set. Feel free to use “wave” loading as well.

12334.details:
8 Rounds for Time:
4 Strict Pull Ups
12 Air Squats
24 Double Unders
12334.notes:
Intent <12 minutes
Scale so each round can be completed <1:30 (not just the first round!)
What’s the fastest speed you can move today while maintaining full ranges of motion on each rep?
Pull Up Scaling
RX+. 4 Strict Chest to Bar
A. 2-3 Strict
B. 4 Box Pike OR Band Assisted Strict
Double Under Scaling (30 sec max per round)
A. 12-16 DU
B. 30 sec Practice

12335.notes:
In 15 minutes, build to a heavy, technically sound double on the power clean and jerk. This is not necessarily a max.
After the first rep, bail the bar and reset on the floor. Take 5-10 seconds before starting the second rep.

12335.details:
AMRAP 7 MIN
3-6-9-12-15-etc.
Clean and Jerks 135/95/65#
Toes to Bar
12335.notes:
From the annals of Crossfit Open history! If you’re an OG, check your notes from 2013 and see if you can get some more work done today.
Intent > 4 rounds of work (finishing the round of 12 or more). Scale loading, volume, or movement complexity as needed!
The barbell should be moderate for you, something you could cycle a few reps with, but will likely choose singles in the workout itself.
Using 60-70% of your heaviest double today is a decent guideline.
TTB Scaling
A. Volume: 2-4-6-8-10-etc. OR 1-3-5-7-etc.
B. Range of motion: toes to eye level or chest level
C. Kipping Knees to Chest
D. V-Ups

12337.details:
A. Bench Press, 3×4-6
B. Back Squat, 3×6-8
C. (2 Squat Snatches + 2 Overhead Squats) x 6-8 Sets
D. Strict Press, 3×8-12
E. Deadlift, 3×6-8
12337.notes:
Tomorrow we have biking, rowing, shuttle runs, and devil’s press 👿
The lifts can be sets across or building. Rep schemes are the same as last week for ABDE, so aim to increase reps in the range if you were at the low end OR increase load if you were maxing out the reps.
Snatch Complex: Beginner lifters should work with light to moderate load and aim for consistency in positions and range of motion. Int/Adv lifters: start at 50% and build by about 5% each set. Feel free to use “wave” loading as well!

12337.details:
2 Intervals
In 3 minutes:
20 Push Ups
20 Alternating DB Box Step Overs
Max Calorie bike in remaining time
Rest 3 Min between intervals
12337.notes:
Hit your first interval with high effort, 90% +
As soon as your rest period starts, aim to slow your breathing, walk/shake the legs out, and get mentally ready to hit it hard again.
Can you beat your bike score in round 2??
Push Ups: Scale volume and/or elevate to complete your reps in 1-3 quick sets. Do not spend more than 1 minute here.
Step Overs: DB: 50/35/20# ea hand
20 total alternating reps, 10 ea side leading. You do not need to stand all the way up on the box today; just get to the other side with both feet.

12338.details:
For Max Reps:
5 min Bike Calories
1 min Rest
5 min Row Calories
1 min Rest
5 min Shuttle Runs (40′)
1 min Rest
5 min Alternating Single Arm Devil’s Presses
12338.notes:
This looks like a series of short workouts, but go into it with the 23′ total timestamp in mind. Work hard near your threshold, but be wary of flying too close to the sun early on this one.
1 rep on the shuttle run = 40′ segment = “down and back.” You might want a whiteboard here with hash marks to keep track of your reps!
DB: 50/35/20#. Choose a moderately heavy weight that you’re comfortable steadily cycling from side to side.

12338.details:
Sandbag Bear Hug Hold
Accumulate 4 min in as few sets as possible with a heavy bag.

12339.details:
Every 2:30 min x 8 Sets
2 Squat Cleans + 30 Sec Bike
12339.notes:
The focus and intent here is technique on the lift, albeit under a bit of fatigue. Start with a conversational pace on the bike. Dial you intensity up or down depending on your experience level and tolerances.
New lifters: Moderate loads throughout to build mechanics and consistency.
Int & Adv: Start at 50-60% of your best clean. Add ~5% to the bar each set, working up towards 85% +. If you miss a lift, repeat or decrease load and wave up again.

From the floor. You can squat clean the first rep OR power clean, get settled, and begin.
If you’re not sure where to start, drop weight from where you finished your cleans and work to RPE 8.5/10 by the final set.
Another guideline is about 80% of what you did for last week’s back squats in the same rep range.
Focus on:
-active shoulders, creating a “shelf” for the bar to rest on
-braced core
-bar staying over mid-foot

12340.details:
A1. DB Strict Press, 4-5 x 8-12, building or across
A2. Strict Chin Up, 4-5 x max reps
12340.notes:
Rest about 45 sec after pressing and 1:30-2:00 after chin ups.
Do at least one lighter/shorter warm up set before the work sets.
Press: Refer back to Week 1. Rep range is same, so try to increase either volume, load, or both!
Chin Ups: If you hit 10+ reps in Week 1 across all your sets, add weight today.
If you are not yet doing sets of 5+ reps unbroken, use the progression below. Aim to do more total reps than in Week 1:
A. Bodyweight “Cluster sets”, aiming for 6-8 reps per set (ex: 4+3 or 3+2+1, with short rest between)
B. Negatives, 4 x 3, as slow as possible
C. Box Pike or Foot Assisted, 4 x 5-8

12340.details:
For Time:
1000/800m Row
20 Strict Dips
200 Double Unders
20 Push Ups
12340.notes:
Intent <12 min
Row <4 min. Scale volume further if needed.
DU Scaling
A. 100
B. 60 — count attempts/misses as well as makes
C. 3 min DU attempts
Dip/Push Up Scaling: choose two variations (first harder, second easier) that you can do at least 5+ unbroken when fresh:
-Ring Dip
-Matador Dip
-Deficit Push Up
-Push Up
-Elevated Push Up
No bands for this particular workout. If needed, elevated push ups can be done twice.

12341.details:
Every 3:30 x 5 Rounds
6 Deadlifts 225/155/105#
8 Bar Facing Burpees
10/8/6 Cal Bike
12341.notes:
Intent < 1:40/Round.
Attack each round. Set up well for your deadlift, find your most efficient method for burpees, and transition to the bike as quickly as possible. Scale load, volume, or movement complexity to stay under the timestamp goal, working at a high effort.
DL: Moderate load, unbroken. ~55-65% of a 1 RM.
BFB Scaling:
A. 6 Reps
B. 4-6 Reps, step over the bar
Bike: <45 sec at high effort. Scale calories further as needed.

12341.details:
3-4 Rounds for Quality
15 Hollow Rocks
10 Slider Hamstring Curls

12344.details:
A. Bench Press, 3×4-6
B. Back Squat, 3×6-8
C. (2 Squat Cleans + 2-4 Front Squats) x 6-8 Sets
D. Strict Press, 3×8-12
E. Deadlift, 3×6-8
12344.notes:
Tomorrow we have burpee box jump overs, wall ball, handstand push up, and thrusters.
The lifts can be sets across or building. The rep schemes are the same as last week for ABDE, so aim to increase reps in the range if you were at the low end OR increase load if you were maxing out the reps.
Clean Complex: Beginner lifters: work with light to moderate load and aim for consistency in positions and range of motion. Int/Adv lifters: start at 50-60% and build by about 5% each set. Feel free to use “wave” loading as well!

12344.details:
3 Rounds for Time:
270m Run
15 Chest to Bar Kipping Pull Ups
30 Barbell Back Rack Reverse Lunge @ 45/35/22#
12344.notes:
Intent <14 min
This workout will largely be a challenge to our kipping technique efficiency and endurance. The run/row and lunges are short and light on purpose… you’ll be back to that rig before you know it. Plan accordingly, breaking the pull-ups into manageable sets so you’re never on the edge of failure.
Run <1:30/rd — if you’re feeling a bit too chilly today, complete a 300m Row OR 600m Bike instead.
Pull-ups: Full volume is appropriate if you have 8+ unbroken chest to bar reps. Choose a scaling optoion you can complete in 2-4 tough sets.
Pull Up Scaling
A. 7-10 Kipping CTB
B. 10-15 Kipping Pull Up (chin over)
C. 8 Strict (CTB or chin over)
D. 10-15 TOUGH ring rows
Lunges: Light weight. Ideally unbroken, resting at the top as needed.

12348.details:
For Time:
6 Rounds (3 Each)
8 Burpee Box Jump Overs
12 Wall Ball Shots
6 Rounds (3 Each)
8 Burpee Box Jump Overs
12 Handstand Push Ups
6 Rounds (3 Each)
8 Burpee Box Jump Overs
12 Dumbbell Thrusters @ 50/35/20# ea
12348.notes:
Intent < 30 min
Partners trade full rounds of work on each couplet.
A completes BBJO+WB
B completes BBJO+WB
Back and forth for 3 rounds each, 6 total.
Then they move on in the same fashion to the HSPU couplet, and so forth.
BBJO: 24/20/16″. Face the box at the bottom of each burpee. Scale to a box height, rep count, and method (jump/step) you can complete in 50 seconds or less consistently.
WB: 20#,10′ / 14#,9′ / 10#,8′ . Scale for unbroken sets.
Thruster: Scale for unbroken sets.
HSPU: Strict or Kipping. Prerequisite to kip is at least 1 strict rep to the range of motion you’re using in the workout!
HSPU Scaling (1-2 sets per round):
A. 6-10 reps, up to 1 abmat
B. 6-10 Box Piked
C. 6-10 DB Strict Press
D. 6-10 Push Ups

12349.details:
A. Bench Press, 3×4-6
B. Back Squat, 3×6-8
C. (2 Squat Cleans + 2-4 Front Squats) x 6-8 Sets
D. Strict Press, 3×8-12
E. Deadlift, 3×6-8
12349.notes:
Tomorrow we have sandbag holds, sled pushing, and some choices around rig work and biking/runing!
The lifts can be sets across or building. The rep schemes are the same as last week for ABDE, so aim to increase reps in the range if you were at the low end OR increase load if you were maxing out the reps.
Clean Complex:
Beg: Light to moderate load and aim for consistency in positions and range of motion.
Int/Adv: Start at 50-60% and build by about 5% each set. Feel free to use “wave” loading as well!

12349.details:
5 Rounds For Time:
8 Single Arm Chainsaw Row – L arm
8 Single Arm Chainsaw Row – R arm
16 Abmat Sit Ups
16 Russian KB Swings
12349.notes:
Intent <13 min
Ideally use 1 Kettlebell for the whole workout. If you’re between weights on the row, a DB can also be used.

12353.details:
30 min for Quality + Load
8 Strict Knees to Elbows OR Strict Pull Ups
40 sec Sandbag Bear Hug Hold
100′ Sled Push
1200m Bike or 400m Run
12353.notes:
Groove on a steady pace today, focusing on quality of movement over intensity.
The gymnastic movement is athlete’s choice today, or you may mix and match, trading off movements each round.
Sandbag: Heavy!
Sled: Moderate weight you can keep moving at a consistent rhythm for the full 100′
If you attend 1-3 days/week, feel free to hit the bike/run a bit harder and keep your transitions tight.
If you attend 4+ days/weeek, this should feel like a comfortable, enjoyable day of training and you leave feeling like you have more in the tank!

12356.details:
Every 2 min x 8 Sets
2 Snatches + 1 Overhead Squat
12356.notes:
Snatches can be power or full today, athlete’s choice. They are not touch and go. After your first rep, reset the bar to the floor and take at least 5 seconds to organize before the second. Keep the bar overhead to continue into your OHS, to the best depth you can control.
Newer lifters: Work with light to moderate loads to build mechanics and consistency on the lift.
Int/Adv: Start around 50-60%. Add ~5% to the bar each set, working up towards 85%+. If you miss a lift, repeat or decrease load and wave up again.

Many athletes have completed this workout in blazing-fast times, but don’t let that deter you from attempting the prescribed version.
The load of the barbell should allow you to perform at least 7 unbroken deadlifts every time you pick it up. Reduce the load to achieve this stimulus and, above all, maintain the integrity of the lift.
The handstand push-up option you choose should allow you to complete at least 5 reps every time you kick up. Reduce the difficulty as suggested below. If scaling, your variation should not allow you to complete the reps unbroken (if you do, the movement is too easy).

A. 15-9-6 HSPU
B. 21-15-9 Box Piked
C. 15-9-6 Box Piked
C. 21-15-9 DB Strict Press

12363.details:

Sets 3-4: 3 Squat Cleans + 30 Sec Bike

2 sets @ 60-70%
2 sets @ 70-80%
2 sets @ 80-90%+
The goal is always to make every lift, so adjust based on how things are grooving today. If you miss a lift, repeat or decrease load and wave up again.

From the floor. You can squat clean the first rep OR power clean, get settled, and begin.
Reference your notes from Week 3 (same scheme) and aim to increase reps or loading today. If you’re not sure where to start, drop weight from where you finished the cleans and work to RPE 8.5/10 by the final set.
Focus on:
-active shoulders creating a “shelf” for the bar to rest on
-braced core
-bar staying over midfoot

250m Row -OR- 500m Bike
8 Alternating DB Suitcase Reverse Lunges @ 50/35/20# ea
8 Burpee to Target
12376.notes:
Intent < 21 min.
Row/Bike: <1:15/round. Find a challenging pace that still allows you to get right off the machine and immediately into your lunges. Scale meters back as needed to stay within the time domain.
Lunges: 1 DB each hand. Heavy load. Make sure to stand all the way up on each rep, opening knee and hip joints completely and stacking the head and shoulders on the rest of the body.
Burpee: Find a pull-up bar that is above your standing reach, ideally 4-6″. Touch with both hands at the top of each rep.

10-15 DB Lying Tricep Extensions
10-15 ea Side Plank Raises
12376.notes:
Curls: 7 reps full extension to 90 degrees + 7 reps 90 degrees to full flexion + 7 reps full rep!
Rest 30-45 seconds between movements. Adjust loading as needed.

12377.details:

12377.notes:

PU: Jumping Pull Ups, Banded Pull Ups (5/round), Ring Rows
Shuttle Run:
1 Rep = 40′ = 20′ down and 20′ back.
Complete 5 reps, or scale to a number you can finish at a tough effort pace under 40 seconds.

12385.notes:

All reps of the pull ups must be completed before moving onto the push ups, and so forth.
Today is a perfect day to develop virtuosity in movement — doing the common uncommonly well. These are simple calisthenics; potent if executed at our threshold pace. How quickly can you move while completing each of your 400 reps with full range of motion and consistent mechanics?
Aim to avoid any one exercise taking more than 8 minutes.
If you are scaling and you can complete more than 15 reps at a time of your pull/push variation, it’s too easy. Use the placement of your feet on ring rows and the height of your barbell or box on the push ups to find that “just right” level of difficulty today.

60 pull-ups
60 push-ups
100 sit-ups
100 squats
Scaling Option B

60 elevated push-ups
80 sit-ups
80 squats

12391.notes:

Rest about 45-60 sec after bench press, and about 1-2 minutes after rows.

6-8 ea Contralateral DB/KB Single Leg Romanian Deadlift

12392.notes:
Jump Rope: Work on something you are not already good at. Here are some ideas/strategies…
DU ninja: Mess around with Crossovers today.
Inconsistent Double Underer: Pick a number and aim to do a few sets of that consistently. An athlete who has done 20 reps total consecutively as a max effort might choose to do 3 x 12, with 10-15 sec rest between sets.
Single-Double-Single-Double: Do a ladder. 1 DU, stop. 2 DU, stop. 3 DU, etc. Force yourself to practice small numbers of consecutive reps.
No Dubs Yet: Do 1-2 rounds of 30 sec each wrist rotations + 30 sec tall pogo hops without the rope. Then work on putting it together! Try really freakin’ hard!

40 WB Shots (choose weight/height)
40 Burpee Box Step Ups (choose height)

Partners alternate full rounds of work. In each section, each partner does 2 rounds, adding up to 4 total as a team.
In this workout, the gymnastics get more advanced and the barbell weight increases as fatigue accumulates. Choose variations that will progressively challenge you, appropriate to your skill level and tolerances today!
Gymnastics: Pick 3 movements along the list below. If you prefer, you could also just stick with one skill you are aiming to build your efficiency on (for example: chin over bar kipping pull-ups).
Ring Rows
Jumping Pull Ups
Band Assisted Strict Pull Ups
Strict Pull Ups
Kipping Pull Ups
Strict Chest to Bar Pull Ups
Kipping CTB Pull Ups
Bar Muscle Ups
DU Scaling:
A. 20 sec practice/round
B. 30 Single Unders
Thrusters: Choose progressively heavier loading for each section that you can complete in 1-2 sets.

12418.details:
A. Bench Press, 3×4-6
B. Back Squat, 3×4-6
C. (2 Squat Cleans + 2-4 Front Squats) x 4-6 Sets
D. Strict Press, 3×6-10
E. Deadlift, 3×4-6
12418.notes:
Tomorrow we have renegade rows, lunges, shuttle runs, and a bi/tri cashout!
ABDE lifts are the same rep schemes as last week. The lifts can be sets across or building.
Clean Complex: Use prior weeks as guidance on loading. Start moderate and build as you’re able across the sets. If you fail a rep, come back down in load and “wave” up again.

12418.details:
For Time
40/32 Cal Row
40 Push Ups
40/32 Cal Bike
40 Sit Ups
12418.notes:
Intent < 14 min
Row and Bike < 3:00 each. Scale rep counts back if needed.
Chip, chip, chip away at this one! Maintain virtuosity and full ranges of motion in your bodyweight movements as you fatigue.
Push Up Scaling: RX is appropriate if you can do 8+ reps unbroken when fresh.
A. 30 Push Ups
B. 40 Elevated
C. 30 Elevated
*If scaling to elevated, choose a height you can do about 6-8 reps when fresh. If you can do more than that at once, it’s too easy.

12419.details:
Every 3 Min x 5 Rounds
8 Alt Renegade Rows
8 Alt DB Front Rack Reverse Lunge
Max Reps Shuttle Run up to 1:30 mark
12419.notes:
Intent: Heavy weight that you can slog through both movements without having to break them up. You should have at least 30 sec for shuttle runs per round, if not more.
DB: 50/35/20# ea hand. The movements are 8 reps total, 4 ea side.
1 Rep of the Shuttle Run = 20′ down + 20′ back (40′ total).
Goal is to work at a consistent, challenging pace for consistent scores across the rounds (+/- a shuttle run or two).

12419.details:
2 Rounds to Failure
Max Reps Supinated Grip DB Bicep Curls
Rest 1 min
Max Reps Single DB Overhead Tricep Extension
Rest 1 min
12419.notes:
Take a warm up round to suss out a weight you can get at least 10 reps on each movement.
Then complete 2 rounds as written, going all the way to failure on each movement, each round. Don’t hold back.
It’s normal/expected to have some attrition on the second round!
*If you’re feeling beat up from Saturday’s pull-up heavy WOD, skip the curls and choose a core movement instead for 15-20 reps (v-ups, tuck ups, sit-ups).

12426.details:
Every 2:30 min x 8 Sets
Sets 1-2: 30 Sec Bike + 4 Snatches
Sets 3-4: 30 Sec Bike + 3 Snatches
Sets 5-6: 30 Sec Bike + 2 Snatches
Sets 7-8: 30 Sec Bike + 1 Snatch
12426.notes:
Snatches may be Power OR Squat. Athlete’s choice!
This is the same structure from Week 5, when we did this with Cleans. This will feel metabolically taxing, but ideally you’ll get more rest as you complete less reps, so you can continue to recharge your battery for the heavier sets! Try to find a “just-hard-enough” effort on the bike to challenge your lifting. If you were here in Week 5, refer back to your calorie counts / notes to help you.
Newer lifters: Start light and aim to build a bit across the 8 sets.
Int & Adv: Suggested loading below, or use your notes from this cycle to guide you.
2 sets @ 50-60%
2 sets @ 60-70%
2 sets @ 70-80%
2 sets @ 80-90%+
If you miss a lift, repeat or decrease load and wave up again.

Aim to add load or reps to what you did in Week 6! These should be tough sets, with no more than 1 rep in reserve.
Focus on creating as much speed as possible out of the bottom of your squat.

12429.details:
A1. Bench Press 3×4-6
A2. Three Point DB Row 3×8-12 ea
12429.notes:
Bench Press: Take 3-4 progressive warm up sets before your work sets. Leave 0-1 Reps in Reserve today.
On both exercises, aim to go heavier or get more reps than in Week 6. If you haven’t tried the next DB weight up… today’s the day, friend!!!

12431.details:
4 Rounds for Time
400m Run
16 DB Hang Power Clean and Jerk @ 50/35/20#
16 Tuck Ups
12431.notes:
Intent <17 min
If your run pace will be over 2:30/400m, scale to 270m.
The hang clean and jerk is 16 total reps. Suggested method is either 8L/8R or trading off every 4 reps.
You may strict press, push press, or jerk the overhead portion of the movement, as long as the hips and knees fully extend while the DB is still overhead.
For the tuck ups, start and finish in a hollow body position and come to the tailbone in the middle of each rep.

12431.details:
3-5 Sets
1:00 Sandbag Bear Hug Hold
:30 each Side Plank
12431.notes:
Use the heaviest sandbag you can for a minute unbroken hold.
Add a DB or KB to your side plank or do a Star Plank to level up here!

12434.details:
A. Bench Press, 3×4-6
B. Back Squat, 3×4-6
C. Snatch x 4-3-2-2-1-1
D. Strict Press, 3×6-10
E. Deadlift, 3×4-6
12434.notes:
Tomorrow we have 25.1! Burpees, DB hang clean-to-overheads, and walking lunges.
ABDE lifts are the same rep schemes as last week. The lifts can be sets across or building.
Snatch: Can be Power or Squat, athlete’s choice! Based on Tuesday’s workout, use the rep scheme provided to work up towards a heavy-ish single today. The multi-rep sets are not intended as touch and go. Reset on the floor and take your time for each rep.

12434.details:
4-5 Rounds for Quality
3-6 Chin-Ups
9 Ball Slams
12 Air Squats
15/12 Cal Bike or Row
12434.notes:
For those coming to class to hit Open WOD 25.1 tomorrow, focus on quality movement and low to moderate intensity today.
If you’re resting tomorrow, feel free to hit this a bit harder and work at a faster pace!
If you were not in class yesterday and prefer to swap in some running and/or tuck-ups to this workout, go for it.
Chin Ups: Scale up by going chest to bar and/or adding weight. Scale down by using a band, foot assist, or electing for ring rows instead.

*After completing each round, add 3 reps to the burpees and hang clean-to-overheads.

12437.notes:
Review the Workout Standards and common faults for each movement.
Be bold, be brave, work hard, cheer for your fellow athletes, and make yourself proud!

12435.details:
A. Bench Press, 3×4-6
B. Back Squat, 3×4-6
C. Snatch x 4-3-2-2-1-1
D. Strict Press, 3×6-10
E. Deadlift, 3×4-6
12435.notes:
Tomorrow we have strict pull-ups, double unders, DB bench press, and cyclist squats.
ABDE lifts are the same rep schemes as last week. The lifts can be sets across or building.
Snatch: Can be Power or Squat, athlete’s choice! Based on Tuesday’s workout, use the rep scheme provided to work up towards a heavy-ish single today. The multi-rep sets are not intended as touch and go. Reset on the floor and take your time for each rep.

12435.details:

12435.notes:
Intent <14 min
Both partners work at the same time on this one. While Partner A is completing 1 round of the couplet, Partner B is rowing for meters. When 1 round is complete, switch places. Continue in this fashion, and keep your transitions tight.
The workout is complete when each partner has done 5 rounds of the couplet (10 total) and the team has reached 2000m total on the erg!
One individual round of the couplet should not exceed 1:30. If needed, scale back height of the box and/or volume of work, for example:
8 Box Jumps, 16″
12 Sit Ups

12440.notes:
Intent <12 min
If strict pull-ups and double unders are not yet developed, intensity is less important than facilitating practice and technical refinement. If you are proficient in these movements, attempt to finish quickly with minimal breaks.
Pull-Up Scaling:
A. 2-4-6-8-10
B. Banded or Box Assist, full volume or 2-4-6-8-10
DU Scaling:
A. 40-30-20-10-5
B. 30 sec Practice after each set of pull-ups

12440.details:
3-4 Progressive Sets
8-10 DB Bench Press @ 20X1
8-10 Goblet Slantboard Squats @ 20X1
12440.notes:
Start with moderate loads you are confident holding the tempo on and work progressively heavier across your sets as technique allows.
Superset the two movements, resting as needed between each.

12441.notes: Build to a heavy triple for the day.

12441.details:
4 Rounds for Quality
16 Front Foot Elevated DB Suitcase Reverse Lunges
1:00 Row for Average Watts
1:00 Arch hold
12441.notes:
Rest as needed between the movements to find a heavy load on the lunges, strong effort on the row, and high quality for the arch hold.
Lunge: Use one to two 45’s plates for your lunge set up. Ideally find a height that puts you bellow parallel at the bottom of the rep.
Row: Set up monitor to watts. In your first round, row at a moderate effort. Allow the flywheel to roll to a stop and note your average watts for the minute. Increase your avg watts as you move from round to round.
Arch: Active tissue from fingertips to toes!

12449.details:
12 Rounds for Time
10 Wall Ball Shots (20#/10′, 14#/9′, 10#/8′)
10 Kipping Toes to Bar
12/10 Cal Bike
12449.notes:
Intent <21 min, where each individual round is under 1:45. Scale load, volume, or movement complexity to achieve that consistently.
Partners alternate full rounds of work, 12 total, 6 each. You should start this at a relatively hot pace, keeping transitions tight and starting with a bike effort that feels tough, but not maximal.
TTB Scaling
A. 5 Strict
B. 5-8 Kipping, full ROM
C. 10 Partial ROM (Hanging Leg Raise)
D. 10 V-Ups/Tuck-Ups

12453.details:
For Load
Shoulder Press 1-1-1-1-1
Push Press 3-3-3-3
Push Jerk 5-5-5
12453.notes:
Today’s workout is a classic heavy day. Even though most athletes can perform this workout as prescribed, the challenge lies in the technical complexities of the movements. Adding load should be based on your ability to stay mechanically sound. Each athlete, regardless of experience, should focus on technique first and foremost.
Scaling:
Reduce the load on the barbell to maintain the safety and integrity of each lift.
In case of injury or limitation, perform a single-arm dumbbell shoulder press, push press, and push jerk.

12454.details:
A. Bench Press, 3×3-5
B. Deadlift, 3×3-5
C. Back Squat, 3×3-5
D. Push Press, 4×3
E. Power Clean, 4×3
12454.notes:
Tomorrow we have Open Workout 25.2, which includes pull-ups, chest to bar pull-ups, bar muscle-ups, double unders, and thrusters.
On the powerlifting options today, you can go sets across or build. Get some relatively heavy weight moving but focus on smooth, controlled descents and fast, powerful ascents for each rep.
For the push press and power clean, use weights that allow you refine your technique.

12454.details:
3-4 Rounds for Quality
:30 ea Side plank
1:00 Bike
:30 ea Single Arm Farmer Carry
270m Run or 500m Row
12454.notes:
Move and groove. Even though this is for quality, minimize transition time and stay focused on continuous, low intensity work.
If you’re doing the Open Workout tomorrow, take your bike and run/row at a recovery pace, ideally breathing through your nose. If not, feel free to hit those conditioning elements a bit harder and keep your transitions tight to create a more challenging stimulus.
Side Plank: Scale up by adding a DB/KB hold or doing Star Plank.

12455.details:

21 Pull-ups

36 Double-Unders

30 Double-Unders

12455.notes:
Repeat Open workouts are a great way to check in on how our fitness is progressing over time. Remember that any given day of training (or competition) is just a snapshot. It doesn’t tell the whole story. Whether it’s your first or second time with this one, make a strategy that works for you, work hard, and be proud of your effort today.
This workout is pretty similar to one we did partner-style on Saturday, Feb 22! It will add up quickly without the built-in rest and more reps in each set, so break things up according to your abilities and chip your way through it.

45, 65, 85 lb

12456.details:
EMOM x 32 Min
A. 14/11 Cal Row
B. 6 Sandbag Ground to Shoulder
C. 40 Sec Shuttle Run
D. 15-20 Tuck ups
12456.notes:
It’s a long one!
Each station < 40 sec. Scale rep counts, load, or movement complexity as needed.
Your first two rounds should feel very manageable — not exactly a conversational pace, but very in control and nowhere near your “threshold.” Effort will have to increase as fatigue accumulates in order to sustain your rep counts and paces across the 8 rounds.
If you did the Open workout yesterday, scale back a bit today. Your goal should be to get a good sweat, move with high quality, not be stressed out for 32 minutes, and leave feeling better than you walked in 🙂

12458.details:
Every 4 Min x 4 Sets for Load and Times
8 Bench Press
300/250m Row
12458.notes:
Score for this workout is total weight lifted (don’t worry, Beyond the Whiteboard will calculate it for you!) and the total time of your four rowing intervals.
At 3,2,1… Go, begin your set of bench press. Re-rack the bar and move with intent to the erg. Work at a hard effort and note the time to complete your row distance. Your goal is to have 4 row efforts with are pretty similar outcomes and as little time as possible. In other words, try to find your hardest recoverable pace!
If desired, set the erg to count down your meters: Menu>Select Workout>New Workout>Single Distance, and then toggle until you get the right number!
On each subsequent round: Menu>Select Workout>ReRow!

12458.details:
3-5 Rounds for Quality
1:00 Handstand Hold
16-20 Alternating Hand-to-Hand KB Swings
12458.notes:
Rest as needed to keep quality on both movements.
Handstand: Accumulate time as needed. You can kick-up or do a wall walk to hold a wall-facing inversion. Advanced athletes can accumulate time in a free-standing hold.
KB: Choose a moderate load that allows you to practice good timing and coordination on this swing variation.

12461.notes: Take 2-3 warm up sets and then 5 work sets with the front squat today. Use a slower-down, faster-up tempo. Build towards a heavy triple, leaving 1 rep in reserve.

12461.details:
4 Rounds For Quality
6-10 Strict Toes to Bar
12 Alternating Single DB Box Step Ups
1:00 Arch Hold
12461.notes:
TTB: It’s highly likely that we’ll see some kipping toes to bar in this week’s Open Workout. Use today to dial in your strict mechanics or if you prefer, use it as practice time to iron out your kip. If choosing kip practice, be mindful of your hands (no tearing!) and keep the sets small.
TTB Options
A. Partial ROM Strict TTB
B. Strict Knees to Elbows
C. Incline Strict TTB
D. Kipping TTB Practice Time!
Box Step Ups: Use a single DB held behind the neck, front rack, or goblet style. Alternate legs for 12 total, 6 each. Fully extend knees and hips at top of each rep.

12464.details:
For Time:
50/40 Cal Assault Bike
21 Deadlifts @ 135/95/65#
21 Burpees
15 Power Cleans
15 Burpees
9 Power Snatches
9 Burpees
12464.notes:
Intent <15 min
Pacing is the key here. Keep your breathing steady throughout the workout.
Stay efficient with your movements—including the burpees. They take a lot of time if you don’t stay smooth. Avoid pausing on the ground.
Prioritize good mechanics over speed. Especially when you’re tired, it’s easy to rush and make mistakes. If you stick to a solid pace, manage your breath, and focus on one movement at a time, you’ll crush it.
Bike < 5 min. Scale calories as needed.
Barbell: Should be very light for deadlift, light to medium for power clean, and moderate for power snatch. The snatch weight should be something you’re confident doing relatively quick singles on. Scale as needed, while aiming to find one weight that works for all three movements.
Burpee Scaling
A. 15/12/9 – Full ROM
B. 21/15/9 – No Push Up

12466.notes:
Accumulate a total of at least 12 quality reps on each side today, more if time allows. Trade arms as desired. Keep your eyes on the weight you’re using and use your core to stabilize your body throughout each rep. Pause for a eat in each phase of the movement to create clear landmarks for yourself with this multi-part exercise.
Beginners: Use light to moderate loads throughout.
Int/Adv: Once you’ve established clear mechanics and consistency at light weights, build in load to something challenging for the day.

400m Run
Max Reps Strict Pull Ups
12466.notes:
This workout is based on the CrossFit benchmark workout “Nicole.”
Intent: 3-5 Rounds
Pull-Up Scaling, based on athlete capacity…
>10 unbroken. If you’re concerned about over-doing it on volume today, you can “cap” your pull-ups in each round. Work to around RPE 8/10, or 2-3 reps in reserve, instead of to failure.
> 5 Reps Unbroken: Perform the workout RX’d.
< 5 Reps Unbroken: Begin each set with a max set of strict pull-ups (yes, 1 counts!), then add a band to get to at least 5 reps each round, ideally more in some rounds.
No Strict Pull Ups (yet!): Perform a version of banded strict pull-ups OR ring rows that allows for a tough set of at least 5 reps.

A. 270m Run
B. Substitution: Bike 1200/1000m or Row 500/400m

12467.notes:

If you’re doing tomorrow’s workout, good options are to front squat at moderate load, make up strict pull-ups if you missed them yesterday, or do low volume cleans or snatches to keep your technique feeling fresh.
Pull-Ups can be weighted, bodyweight, foot-assisted, or band-assisted.

If you’re already comfortable with double unders, work on boxer skips, alternating foot step, varying tempo/height singles, or crossover jump rope!

12468.details:

50 Calorie Row
5 Wall Walks

Check out this rowing pace chart to help you with your strategy on those 50 cals.
If you are not registered for the Open, today could be a great day to challenge yourself on one or several of the movements.
Or… it could be a good day to employ your scaling options and find a manageable method with which to attack this one and hopefully finish it!
Either way, work hard and make yourself proud.

12469.details:
3-5 Sets of the Complex
6-8 Chainsaw Rows – L

20 sec Goblet Bottom-of-Squat Hold
12469.notes:
Use one implement for all three movements and perform them as a connected “complex” without rest.
Then, take 1-2 min rest between sets.
Start with moderate load and build to something very challenging. Using a KB is preferred, but if you find you’re between weights, a DB works, too!
For the squat, hold in your best/deepest active squat, with the elbows off the knees and lumbar curve maintained.

12469.details:

8/6 Cal Bike
12469.notes:
Intent <7 min.
Come out swinging on this one! When you get those special feelings in your legs and lungs in round 3, just remember it’s actually almost over.

12472.details:
Every 2 Minutes for 9 Sets (18 min), Complete:
Advanced:
Power Clean and Push Jerk
(% of 1 RM)
1) 3 reps at 60%
2) 2 reps at 65%
3) 1 rep at 70%
4) 3 reps at 65%
5) 2 reps at 70%
6) 1 rep at 75%

9) 1 rep at 80%

3×115, 2×123, 1×130

Power Clean and Push Jerk x 2 Reps
*Every 3 Sets, Increase weight
12472.notes:
1 “rep” of the complex = 1 Power Clean + 1 Push Jerk. Bail the bar from overhead, reset on the floor, and repeat. Don’t rush between reps.
This cycle we are revisiting the concept of Wave Training in our Olympic lifting! This is the practice of building up in weight, then back down, and back up again, for multiple “waves”. Ideally your technique is very consistent: from the empty bar to heaviest reps.
For the first few weeks of this cycle we’ll wave both the reps and weights to allow you to pay more attention to detail on your technique while still working up to a heavy percentage of your max.
Base your percentages off of whichever lift is your limiting factor. If you’re feeling a bit lit from the Open WOD this weekend, feel free to ignore percentages, go much lighter, and focus on quality movement.

12472.details:
B1. Clean Deadlift, 3×3, building
B2. Seated Arnold Press, 3×10-12 @ 21×1 tempo, building or across
12472.notes:
The Clean Deadlift resembles a standard deadlift to large degree. The critical difference is that the positions, posture and balance match that of a Clean, rather than allowing the higher hips, balance toward the heels, and potentially rounded back of a standard or powerlifting deadlift. Generally, the clean deadlift can start at 90-120% of your best clean. If you are significantly limited by clean technique, you may need to use a heavier percentage to train strength here. Regardless, choose weights you can perform with proper positioning.
Watch the video link to better understand this movement and how to execute it most effectively!
For the press variation, you may build in weight or go sets across. Leave 1-2 good reps in the tank today. Tempo = 2 sec down, 1 sec pause at bottom, “explode” up, 1 sec pause at top.

12475.details:

20 DB Bench Press
20/16 Cal Row
20 Air Squats
20 Kipping Toes to Bar
12475.notes:
Intent 3-5 Rounds.
Bench: Choose a DB weight that you can complete the 20 reps in 2-3 challenging sets. If you can do 20 unbroken it’s too light.

D. 20 Straight Leg Sit Ups

10 ea KB Side Bends

12479.details:
A1. Back Rack Reverse Lunge, 3×6 ea side, Across
A2. KB Gorilla Rows, 3×16-20 Alternating, Building or Across
12479.notes:
Lunges: From the rack. Take 3-4 warm up sets to find a weight that feels like RPE 8/10 for a set of 6. Repeat this weight for 3 total working sets of 6 reps on each side.
You may re-rack the bar and rest briefly between sides if desired.
Rows: Once you’re close to work weight on lunges, do 1 warm up set with light-moderate weight and then 3 working sets, building or across.

12479.details:
7 Rounds for Time
14 KB Swings (32/24/16kg)
7 Burpee Box Jumps (24/20/16″)
12479.notes:
Intent <11 min
Nowhere to hide, really. Be realistic in your approach here and smooth in your first round of burpee box jumps. Going super hard in rounds 1-2 isn’t worth it if you’ll stop with your hands on your knees and slow way down on the back half of your workout.
Be sure to hit full knee and hip extension at the top of each box jump.

A. 5 Burpee Box Jumps
B. 7 No Push-Up Burpee Box Step-Ups

12482.details:
For Time
10,000m Bike
-and at the same time-
10 Rounds of:
80′ Dual KB Farmer Carry (32/24/16kg ea)
80′ Sandbag Bear Hug Carry (100/75/50#)
40′ Each Arm: Single Arm Overhead Carry (32/24/16kg)
12482.notes:
Intent < 22 min
Both athletes are working the whole time today. Partners work together to finish both the bike distance and the carries, alternating after each round of the triplet, as follows:
Partner A completes one round of all three carries while Partner B bikes to chip away at the 10K. Then switch places and continue.
The workout is complete when the bike reads 10000m (or 6.2 miles) and each partner has done 5 rounds of the triplet, 10 total.

and use the other hand for light support at a rig. If balance and technique are rock solid, try one DB in each hand.

12512.notes:
Nope, this isn’t a joke. It’s a CrossFit benchmark/hero workout! Though we need to pace properly to get our best time, this isn’t meant to be a relaxing jog/row sandwich. Set a goal to run a challenging first mile, maintain an uncomfortable pace for the row, and empty the tank on the final mile.

1/2 Mile Run
1000m Row
1/2 Mile Run
Sgt Major Jerry Dwayne Patton, 40, died on 15 October 2008 during High Altitude High Opening (HAHO) training while assigned to Army USSOCOM preparing for deployment to Afghanistan. Jerry is survived by his wife Molly and his sons Chad, Cody, Chase and Connor.

You may re-rack the bar and rest up to 30 sec between sides.

12516.notes: Your coach will take you through a short progression to work on the footwork and foundations of this skill. Renegade Rows: 40 total alternating reps, 20 each side. Moderate load you can complete a big set with… possibly even go unbroken if endurance allows. Maintain midline stabilization throughout: keep a solid plank position with a wide foot stance and stable hips. Resist the urge to break, pike, or tip from side to side.

Score = total number of reps completed in 30 min: calories on bike + row and number of DU’s. You might keep a whiteboard off to the side and after a full round write down your numbers for each station.
Goal is to have a consistent output across 10 rounds (within 1-2 calories and within 5 or so DU’s), knowing that effort will increase as fatigue accumulates.

12613.details:

5,000m Bike

12613.notes:
Intent < 13 min
Both athletes are working the whole time today. Partners work together to finish both the bike distance and the carries/lunges, alternating after each round of the couplet, as follows:
Partner A completes one round carry + lunges while Partner B bikes to chip away at the 5K. Then switch places and continue.
The workout is complete when the bike reads 5000m (or 3.1 miles) and each partner has done 4 rounds of the couplet, 8 total. It’s possible that one element will be complete before the other. Work until both are done!
80′ = 4 x 20′ segments (2 “down-and-backs”)
40′ = 2 x 20′ segments (1 “down-and-back”)
Lunges: Toes start behind one tape line and heels finish beyond the next to clear a 20′ segment. Don’t short it!
Scale loading and distance as needed to finish a challenging workout in under 13 min. Ideally use the same set of KB’s for the carries and lunges. If needed, scale one or both movements so individual rounds don’t take longer than 90 sec.

12615.notes:
In roughly 6-7 total sets, work up to a heavy set of 5 reps, then take your highest successful 5 rep weight, drop to 90% and perform 1 max effort set. The AMRAP should leave you with 1-2 reps in reserve.

45×10
95×8
125×5
145×3

165×5

4 min Burpees to Target
2 min Rest

12617.notes:
This looks like a series of short workouts, but go into it with the 16′ total timestamp in mind. Work hard near your threshold, but be wary of flying too close to the sun early on this one.
Shuttle run: 1 rep = 40′ segment = “down and back.” On each 20′ turnaround, both feet and one hand must touch the floor outside of the tape line. You might want a whiteboard here with hash marks to keep track of your reps.
Burpees: For your target, use a pull-up bar that is above your standing reach. Touch with both hands on each rep. Scale as needed to maintain good mechanics in your movement. One idea would be to do a “full” burpee with chest to floor for the first 2 minutes and then take the push-up portion out for the second 2 minutes.

1 min Sandbag Bear Hug Hold, as heavy as possible

12617.notes: The hollow hold is intentionally not too long of an isometric today, so you can focus on being as “virtuous” in your position as possible. Review the video above for a great visual demonstration as well as some very clear points of performance to aspire to!

12618.details:
Snatch
Intermediate/Advanced: 1 Rep Max
Beginner: 8 x 2, building
12618.notes:
Snatches can be power or full/squat today, athlete’s choice. Keep in mind int/adv lifters will do percentage-based wave loading during this cycle, so you should perform the lift you intend to do most frequently.
If you are brand new to CrossFit, or to this lift, choose the beginner track. Do one set of 2 reps every 2 minutes or so, building in weight as feels appropriate for today and settling in when you find a load that feels like it gives you feedback, and you can still move through clear positions as you explore the technique.
For int/adv lifters, today is a day to see what you can do! Whether or not this is your favorite lift, set yourself up for success. Be intentional with each rep in your warm up and choose a positive mindset before attempting your heavy singles. Some athletes will want to relax, clear their minds, and trust their technique. Others will need to get revved up and just send it. Either way, let’s commit to our lifts and make some memories!

12619.notes: Take 2-3 warm up sets and then 3 work sets at the rep range listed. If you were doing bench press on floater strength days in the last cycle, look back to reference your numbers. Aim to leave 1-2 good reps in the tank on each set.

24/20/16″

12652.details:
For time:
1-mile run
100 pull-ups
200 push-ups
300 air squats
1-mile run
Partition the pull-ups, push-ups, and squats as needed.
If you’ve got a 14/20-lb vest or body armor, wear it.
Expand to see scaling options
Volume Modifications
This simply means decreasing the total number of reps or the distance on the run. A common sub would be to do 3/4 of the volume on the calisthenics or 2/3 distance on each of the mile runs. You can decrease volume across the board, or only on the movements that you struggle most with.
Movement Modifications
If any movement is outside of your ability to perform, even with decreased volume we can easily modify the exercise. Push-Ups can be taken from the knees or elevated, pull-ups can be ring rows or banded and the run can be subbed for a row if needed as well.
Sequence Modifications
Finally, perhaps it’s just the muscular stamina that will catch up to you. For example if Push-Ups are the hardest part of this workout, you can perform 20 rounds of:5 Push-Ups, 5 Pull-Ups, 5 Push-Ups, 15 squats to break up the push-ups into two sets of five.
B. Intermediate

10 Rounds of:

12728.notes:
The first week of this cycle is an opportunity to learn—or reacquaint yourself with—the Sumo Deadlift.
Although the lift has a shorter range of motion compared to the conventional deadlift, many lifters find it more challenging due to its technical demands, especially during the setup and initiation phases. While the Sumo Deadlift is excellent for improving strength balance, it places greater stress on the hips and groin. As a result, expect to reduce your working weights by 10–20% initially as you develop proper form.
Aim for an RPE of 7/10 during your work sets—this means leaving a few reps in reserve and prioritizing good technique over heavy loads. You’ll have the chance to build from week to week as your proficiency and confidence with the lift grow.
If you’re unfamiliar with RPE (Rate of Perceived Exertion), refer to the chart linked for a helpful explanation to guide your training throughout this cycle.
