12741.notes:
Aim for an RPE of 7-8/10 during your work sets—this means leaving a few reps in reserve and perhaps increasing weights slightly from Week 1.
If you’re unfamiliar with RPE (Rate of Perceived Exertion), refer to the chart below for a helpful explanation to guide your training throughout this cycle.

12741.details:
3 Rounds for time:
400 m Run
24 Hand to Hand KB Swings (24/16kg; 12 per arm)
12 Alternating Renegade Rows (6 per arm)
12741.notes:
Today’s metcon is inspired by the classic CrossFit workout “Helen”.
The kettlebell swings may feel more challenging due to the added skill of switching hands. For the renegade rows, choose a weight that’s as heavy as possible while still maintaining a strong plank position throughout.

12744.details:
For Time
Row 250m (x2)
Row 500m (x2)
Row 750m (x2)
Row 500m (x2)
Row 250m (x2)
12744.notes:
This one’s a repeat. Track back to 11/26/23
Each partner does each interval in this workout. Partner A rows 250, then partner B rows 250, Partner A rows 500, etc.
For many pairs, it will be about a 20 minute interval workout. Save a little energy for the back half of this one. It’s potent.
Reset the monitor at the start of each transition so you get a fresh start. Work on continuing to row well as you row harder!

12744.details:
3 Sets
8-12 DB Pullovers
8-12 DB Bicep Curls
10-15 Banded Tricep Pushdown
12744.notes: Start with moderate loads you know you can move well for the rep ranges, and adjust up or down as needed.

12745.details:
Every 90 sec x 12 min (4 Rounds):
Even: Strict Handstand Push-Ups*
Odd: Dual KB Farmers Carry x 45-60 sec
*Alternate Movements each interval for 4 of each, 8 total intervals.
12745.notes:
*Work along the following HSPU progression, listed here from more advanced to more foundational:
A. Max Reps (1-2 RIR)
B. Accumulate Singles
C. Accumulate 2-3 Negatives (3 sec down)
D. Box Piked x Max Reps (1-2 RIR)
E. Tempo DB Press x 10 @ 21X1
If accumulating singles/negatives, keep your work period to about 1 min, so you have time to rest/transition.
If you have…
> 10 unbroken reps: consider adding a deficit.
3-10 unbroken reps: perform A.
< 3 unbroken reps: perform B.
0 strict reps: perform C, D, or E, whichever allows for full ROM practice and controlled movement.
Note your reps this week; goal is to add a rep each round in the following exposure.

12745.details:
For Time
90 Cal Bike
40 Wall Walks
12745.notes:
In this workout, both partners will be working the entire time. Divide the work as desired, trading back and forth as you like.
For example: Athlete A performs 5 wall walks while Athlete B accumulates calories on the bike, then switch places.
It’s possible that the work will not be finished at the same time. For example, if you complete the total wall walks first and have bike calories left over, trade on and off the bike to chip through that as quickly as you can!
Bike: If your team’s average pace is less than 7 cal/min, consider scaling total rep count down.
Wall Walks: If you’re not comfortable doing 4+ full range of motion reps in a minute, scale along this progression:
A. 24-30 full ROM reps (12-15 each)
B. 20 partial ROM reps (10 each)
C. 20 body tightener to angled wall hold (10 each), holding a beat at the top of each rep before walking down with control

12748.details:
3-5 Progressive Rounds for Load & Quality:
20-30s/side Side Plank Hold
6-8 ea Contralateral Single Leg RDL
12-16 Alternating Tall Kneeling Rotational Med Ball Slam, 6-8ea
1:00 Row, Bike, or Jog
12748.notes:
Move at a moderate intensity and load, given that you’ve got some heavy lifting on the back end. Use a single DB or KB for the RDL.
Ball: Use a 6, 8, or 10# ball. Focus on power with each rep, trying to break the floor!

12748.details:
A. Back Squat, 4 x 6-8
B. Sumo Deadlift, 4 x 6-8
C. Bench Press, 4 x 6-8
D. Strict Pull-Ups, 4-5 x Max Reps (1 RIR)
12748.notes:
Tomorrow we have overhead squats and chest to bar pull-ups.
You may superset your main lift with another DB/KB or bodyweight movement.
Pull-Ups: Use the following progression to guide you:
If you have…
> 10 unbroken reps: consider adding load.
5-10 unbroken reps: perform as written.
< 5 unbroken reps: perform a cluster of sub-maximal reps for you with short rest between. For example: 3+2+2 or 2+1+1, with 15-20 sec of rest
0 body weight reps: perform 6-8 box pike or toe assisted reps per set, using as little lower body help as possible to achieve full ROM

12751.details:
AMRAP 20 MIN
2 rounds of:
6 Overhead Squats (95/65 lb)
6 Chest-to-Bar Pull-Ups
Rest 2 min
2 rounds of:
8 Overhead Squats (95/65 lb)
8 Chest-to-Bar Pull-Ups
Rest 2 min
2 rounds of:
10 Overhead Squats (95/65 lb)
10 Chest-to-Bar Pull-Ups
Rest 2 min
2 rounds of:
12 Overhead Squats (95/65 lb)
12 Chest-to-Bar Pull-Ups
*If you finish all 8 rounds, note your time to complete on the running clock! Otherwise note your rounds+reps finished at the buzzer.
12751.notes:
You have 20 minutes to work today, with rest built in. Scale so you can get through at least 6 rounds of work. This will be a tough challenge of pull-up endurance and capacity combined with the mobility and stability challenges of the overhead squat.
OHS: light load. Scale to a weight you’re comfortable doing 10+ reps unbroken with when fresh. This might mean using an empty barbell or training bar.
Pull-Ups:
A. CTB half volume each round (3 / 4 / 5 / 6)
B. CTB for as long as possible, then switch to chin-over-bar
C. Kipping Chin Over Bar
D. Jumping CTB
*PSA: Don’t rip your hands!! If you feel your hand moving a lot on the bar, it means you’re likely going to rip. More movement = more friction = sad hands. Adjust your grip, tighten up your kip swing, shorten your rep scheme, or scale so you don’t rip. Live to train another day!

12753.details:
A. Back Squat, 4 x 6-8
B. Sumo Deadlift, 4 x 6-8
C. Bench Press, 4 x 6-8
D. Strict Pull Ups, 4-5 x Max Reps (1 RIR)
12753.notes:
Tomorrow we have cleans, DB power cleans, push ups, and shuttle runs.
You may superset your main lift with another DB/KB or bodyweight movement.
Pull-Ups: Use the following progression to guide you:
If you have…
> 10 unbroken reps: consider adding load.
5-10 unbroken reps: perform as written.
< 5 unbroken reps: perform a cluster of sub-maximal reps for you with short rest between. For example: 3+2+2 or 2+1+1, with 15-20 sec of rest
0 body weight reps: perform 6-8 box pike or toe assisted reps per set, using as little lower body help as possible to achieve full ROM

12753.details:
Press & Sled Superset
3-4 rounds for Load & Quality
8-10 per side DB Twist Press
Rest 30 seconds
80′ Sled Push
Rest 60-90 seconds
12753.notes:
3-4 rounds for quality, building in weight gradually on the press.
Twist press demands a lot of stabilization, so start light and make small weight increases each round.
Sled push make your first set a primer/warm up, then work with something heavy for your remaining rounds that you can move continuously for 80′ (with just a quick turnaround reset!)

12754.notes:
The 3-position clean consists of three consecutive cleans performed from different starting positions. This week’s sequence is: High hang → Below the knee → From the floor. You may perform squat or power cleans for today’s complex.
The goal of the complex is to reinforce proper pulling technique as you progress from the high hang down to the floor. Pause briefly at the start of each rep to show control and balance with the barbell. This complex will challenge your grip, so consider starting with lighter weights—around 60–75% of your 1RM—before increasing the load.

12754.details:
AMRAP 12:00
8 Dual DB Power Cleans
8-15 DB Push Ups
400 m Run
12754.notes:
The goal today is to choose a load that feels heavy for the DB Power Cleans, but not so heavy that you need to break up your reps.
For the push-ups, aim to complete them in no more than 1-2 sets at any point during the workout. Performing push-ups on dumbbells can allow for a slightly greater range of motion at the bottom, but be mindful not to lose midline stability or alter your elbow positioning. Your elbows should track at about a 45-degree angle from the torso — not flared out wide or pinned tightly to your sides.

12757.notes:
For the past two weeks, we’ve been building up through our sets to find our working weights.
If you were here last week, use those weights to perform sets across at an RPE of 8/10. You’ll likely use a load from sets 2-4 from last week, depending on how heavy you went.
If you have missed the last two exposures, build to a heavy set of six reps, leaving 1-2 reps in reserve (RIR). Prioritize form throughout, especially if you’re newer to this lift.

12757.details:
3-4 Rounds for Quality:
:30 L-Sit
65m each arm Single Arm Farmer Carry (Heavy)
6-8 each leg Cobra Rear Foot Elevated Split Squat @ 41×1
12757.notes:
Work up through the triplet trying to go a little heavier each round on the carry if possible.
The Cobra Rear Foot Elevated Split Squats are intended to challenge your balance and mobility. Note the LONG tempo for each rep with a pause at the bottom and top of the movement.
L-Sits: Scale by accumulating time in shorter sets with quick rest between, tucking one or both legs in, or elevating to a matador hold.

12758.details:
6 rounds, 1 min per station, for max reps of:
Row Calorie
Burpee
Double Under
Rest 1 min
*Rotate immediately to the next station every 1 min; the clock does not stop or reset between stations. Always rest after the jump rope.
12758.notes:
This is a “Fight Gone Bad”-style workout. Former Fittest Man Alive Jeffrey Adler has a logged score of 932 reps on BTWB! He averaged 26 calories, 22 burpees, and 108 DU’s per round. OUCH!
With 3 minutes of work and 1 minute of rest, this will add up quickly for a lot of athletes. Create a strategy today that maximizes your strengths and sets you up for sustaining hard work across all 6 rounds.
Aim for consistent, smooth movement and breathing mechanics. Keep your transitions quick and calm.
Newer or deconditioned athletes should plan to leave themselves a 15-20 second rest/transition in the first couple of rounds until you see how your pace holds up.

12761.details:
Every 90 sec x 12 min (4 Rounds):
A: Strict Pull-Ups*
B: Slider Hamstring Curls x 8-10 @ 30×1
Alternate Movements each interval for 4 of each, 8 total rounds.
12761.notes:
*Choose one strict pulling motion: Pull-ups, Chest to Bar Pull-ups, or Ring Muscle-Ups.
Work along the following progression, listed here from more advanced to more foundational:
A. Max reps (1-2 RIR)
B. Accumulate Singles in 45-60 sec
C. Accumulate 2-3 Negatives in 45-60 sec
D. Toe or Pike Assist x Max reps (1-2 RIR)
In your chosen movement, if you have…
> 10 unbroken reps: consider adding load.
4-10 unroken reps: perform A.
< 4 unbroken reps: perform B.
0 body weight reps: perform C or D
Note your reps this week; goal is to add a rep each round in Week 3.

12761.details:
Every 4:00 x 5 Rounds
10 Alternating DB Power Snatches
:20 Max Wattage Air Bike
12761.notes:
This is a repeat from 11/18/24.
Bike: Your goal is to see how high you can get your wattage and your peak power output, rather than how many meters or cals you achieve. If you max out by the 10-15 sec mark, it’s okay to cool off for the last few seconds. It’s tempting to close your eyes, but try to keep ’em open so you can note your highest number.
You can use the first 2 rounds of this workout to ramp up your intensity.
Snatches: Choose a weight that feels challenging for 10. Think outside the typical 50/35/20# prescriptions today and see what you can do!

12763.details:
A. Back Squat, 4 x 6
B. Sumo Deadlift, 4 x 6
C. Bench Press, 4 x 6
D. Strict Pull Ups, 4-5 x Max Reps (1 RIR)
12763.notes:
Tomorrow we have handstand push-ups, toes to bar, and heavy deadlifts.
You may superset your main lift with another DB/KB or bodyweight movement.
Pull-Ups: Use the following progression to guide you:
If you have…
> 10 unbroken reps: consider adding load.
5-10 unbroken reps: perform as written.
< 5 unbroken reps: perform a cluster of sub-maximal reps for you with short rest between. For example: 3+2+2 or 2+1+1, with 15-20 sec of rest
0 body weight reps: perform 6-8 box pike or toe assisted reps per set, using as little lower body help as possible to achieve full ROM

12763.details:
For Time
21 Sandbag Squats
130m Run
15 Sandbag Squats
270m Run
9 Sandbag Squats
400m Run
12763.notes:
Intent < 9 min
Choose a heavy sandbag weight that you can move in good form through a full depth squat, completing the round of 21 reps in 1-3 sets.

12764.details:
20 Rounds For Time
5 Strict Handstand Push-Ups
5 Strict Toes to Bar
5 Deadlifts 275/185#
12764.notes:
Intent ~16-24 min. Partners alternate full rounds (10 each, 20 total).
Gymnastics movements can be strict or kipping today, athlete’s choice, provided prerequisite strict strength is present before kipping!
RX’d for HSPU is head touching down to the same surface as your hands.
HSPU Scaling
RX+ Deficit (Plates or Parallettes)
A. 2-4 HSPU
B. 5 Box Piked
C. 5 Heavy DB Strict Press
**Limit abmats to max 1. If possible, use a spongy dot or two instead to work as close to full range of motion as possible.
TTB Scaling
A. 3-4 reps
B. 5 Kipping Hanging Leg Raise, toes above hips
C. 5 Kipping Hanging Knee Raise, knees above hips
D. 5 V-Ups
Deadlift: Heavy load given the context of the workout, but nowhere near max. In the realm of 65-75% of 1RM for experienced athletes is a good guideline. Keep in mind you are doing 50 total reps at this weight under fatigue!

12767.details:
A. Back Squat, 4 x 6
B. Sumo Deadlift, 4 x 6
C. Bench Press, 4 x 6
D. Strict Pull Ups, 4-5 x Max Reps (1 RIR)
12767.notes:
Tomorrow we have assistance work, snatch drills, and a snatch complex.
You may superset your main lift with another DB/KB or bodyweight movement.
Pull-Ups: Use the following progression to guide you:
If you have…
> 10 unbroken reps: consider adding load.
5-10 unroken reps: perform as written.
< 5 unbroken reps: perform a cluster of sub-maximal reps for you with short rest between. For example: 3+2+2 or 2+1+1, with 15-20 sec of rest
0 body weight reps: perform 6-8 box pike or toe assisted reps per set, using as little lower body help as possible to achieve full ROM

12767.details:
3-5 sets for load and quality of:
Hand over hand rope pull
Sled Push back
Hand over hand rope pull
Sled Push back
12767.notes:
Track back to 6/15/25.
Pull a sled with the rope, push the sled back. Repeat for a second pull/push set, then rest. Try to increase the load each set, though it should never be so heavy that it stops moving during your pull.
Option to add 1:00 recovery pace bike between sets as you trade off with other athletes in class.
Track back to 3/26/25 for some guidance.

12768.details:
3 Rounds for Quality
1:00 Bike, increase pace each round
5 Seated Box Jumps
3 Hang Snatch High Pulls
3 Hang Muscle Snatch
3 Overhead Squats @ 3111
3 Tall Snatch
12768.notes:
Use these assistance movements as a technique primer for today’s strength work. A few key points:
All the hang work will start from above the knee.
The pull of your muscle snatch should feel similar to the hang snatch high pulls.
The Tall Snatch will start from a flat foot position. You will utilize the same pulling “up” as your high pulls and muscle snatch, but this movement will require you to aggressively change directions to pull under the bar.
Intermediate and Beginner lifters: Start with a lighter barbell than you typically snatch with to dial in tempo and technique.
Advanced lifters: Start with empty bar and either stay there or add light load across the rounds -you will rarely use more than 30-35% of best snatch, and typically lighter is better for quality execution.

12768.details:
Perform 6-8 sets of the complex for load
1 Snatch Pull
1 Hang Snatch from Above the Knee
1 Snatch
12768.notes:
Keep your reps sharp and rest as needed between sets. Today, we encourage full snatches rather than power snatches.
In the snatch pull, focus on fully extending with the bar. During the hang snatch, finish your pull with that same extension before quickly pulling under the bar. Use the final rep of the full snatch practice performing one smooth, continuous movement.
If you’re newer or have limited mobility, you can stick with power snatches. Just add an overhead squat to the last rep to build comfort with the full movement.

12771.notes:
This week, we’re building toward a challenging set of 4–6 reps in four work sets. You’ll likely need several warm up sets before getting started.
If you’re confident in your sumo technique, steer toward the lower end of the rep range and aim to lift heavier than in previous weeks.
If you’re still refining your form, stick with the higher rep range to get more practice at a moderately heavy load.

12771.details:
EMOM x 12 MIN
A. 15/12 Calorie Row
B. 40 sec Shuttle Runs (40′)
C. 8-12 Push Ups + Plank Hold until 40 sec mark
12771.notes:
Row: Aim to hit a consistent number of calories each round that you can complete in about 40 seconds.
Shuttle Runs: One “rep” of shuttle runs will be consider 40′ (2×20′ lengths).
Push Ups: Choose a rep count that you can complete unbroken, and then stay in plank for the remaining time. If you need to scale, elevate to a barbell in a rig to a height you can complete 8-12 reps unbroken, and either stay for your plank or plank on the floor!

12772.details:
2 Rounds
AMRAP 4:00
6 Toes to Bar
24 Double Unders
Rest 4 Min
AMRAP 4:00
40′ DB Suitcase Walking Lunges
80′ Sandbag Carry
Rest 4 Min
12772.notes:
On the first portion, the rep schemes are low volume, with the goal that you’re able to move at a quick clip throughout. The lunge/sandbag section should feel like more of a steady grind.
TTB: Choose a scale that allows you to go unbroken for multiple rounds.
A. 3-4 reps, strict or kip
B. 6 Kipping Leg Raises (toes above hips)
C. 6 Hanging Knee Raises (knees above hips)
DU: < 30 sec/round
A. 10-20
B. 30 sec practice
DB: 50/35/20# ea hand. Heavy, but you should be able to complete 40′ unbroken.
SB: Choose a heavy bag that challenges you. 80′ = 4 x 20′ segments, or “down and back twice!”

12774.details:
Every 90 sec x 12 min (4 Rounds)
Even: Strict Handstand Push-Ups*
Odd: Hip Thrust x 12-15
Alternate Movements each interval for 4 of each, 8 total intervals.
12774.notes:
Hip Thrust: If you’re comfortable with this movement for 15 reps, add a DB at the hips.
HSPU: Work along the following progression, listed here from more advanced to more foundational:
A. Max Reps (1-2 RIR)
B. Accumulate Singles
C. Accumulate 2-3 Negatives (3 sec down)
D. Box Piked x Max Reps (1-2 RIR)
E. Tempo DB Press x 10 @ 21X1
If you have…
> 10 unbroken reps: consider adding a deficit.
3-10 unroken reps: perform A.
< 3 unbroken reps: perform B.
0 strict reps: perform C, D, or E, whichever allows for full ROM practice and controlled movement.
Note your reps this week; goal is to add a rep each round in the following exposure.

12774.details:
21-15-9 Reps for Time of:
Hang Power Clean @ 115/85/65#
*Complete 5 Wall Walks after each round with the barbell
12774.notes:
Intent < 10 min.
For athletes experienced with barbell cycling and comfortable at the wall, this will be a pretty quick workout and should be attacked from the beginning.
For beginner and intermediate athletes, strategically break up your cleans to keep your technique as consistent as possible and stay under your “threshold” before going upside down on wall walks. For example: 8-7-6 or 6-6-5-4.
HPC: Light weight, in the realm of 50-60% is a good guideline for most.
WW:
A. 3 full ROM reps
B. 4-5 partial ROM reps
C. 2 x 15 sec Angled Hollow Body Hold, resting between as needed

12775.details:
A. Back Squat, 4 x 4-6
B. Sumo Deadlift, 4 x 4-6
C. Bench Press, 4 x 4-6
D. Strict Pull Ups, 4-5 x Max Reps (1 RIR)
12775.notes:
Tomorrow we have running, wall balls, box jumps, thrusters, and muscle ups. Wee!
Your main lift can be building or sets across. You may superset with another DB/KB or bodyweight movement if desired.
Pull-Ups: Use the following progression to guide you:
If you have…
> 10 unbroken reps: consider adding load.
5-10 unbroken reps: perform as written.
< 5 unbroken reps: perform a cluster of sub-maximal reps for you with short rest between. For example: 3+2+2 or 2+1+1, with 15-20 sec of rest
0 body weight reps: perform 6-8 box pike or toe assisted reps per set, using as little lower body help as possible to achieve full ROM

12775.details:
3-4 Rounds for Quality
1:00 Rope Climb Practice
1:00 Bike/Row/Run
:30 each side Adductor Side Plank
12775.notes:
Friendly PSA: Learning how to efficiently climb a rope can be brutal for the skin on your legs. We recommend wearing long pants and/or a pair of tall socks or even knee sleeves around your ankles.
Use today’s time to practice your rope climb technique. This video link is set at a point to show a close up of a very efficient footwork method.
Practice Ideas:
A. Rig drill: good to isolate the footwork without worrying about going up the rope.
B. Descent focus: do a partial height climb and practice a safe, controlled descent.
C. Supine to stand climb: Improve upper body strength and grip without footwork.
More experienced athletes: work on completing at 15′ climb in as few “reps” as possible, and/or challenge yourself with how many reps you can complete in 1 minute.
Or… go legless!

12778.details:
For Time
400m Run
50 Wall Ball Shots
400m Run
40 Box Jumps
400m Run
30 DB Thrusters
400m Run
20 Muscle Ups
400m Run
12778.notes:
Intent ~18-26 min. There is a 26 min cap on the workout.
Run: If your pace sets you at > 2:30, scale back to 270m.
Box: 24/20/16″. Scale further to a 12 or 6″ soft box if needed.
WB: 20#, 10′ / 14#, 9′ / 10#, 8′
Mass/center of ball hits above your target line for the rep to count.
Choose a scale that allows you to do 15+ reps unbroken
DB: 50/35/20# ea hand
Tough weight that you can do 6+ reps unbroken
Muscle Ups: Rings or Bar are good to go today. If you’re doing strict ring muscle ups, consider scaling to 10 reps.
MU Scaling:
A. 10 Reps
B. 20 CTB Pull Ups + 20 Dips
C. 20 Pull-ups + 20 Push-Ups
D. 20 Ring Rows + 20 Modified Push ups

12779.details:
A. Back Squat, 4 x 4-6
B. Sumo Deadlift, 4 x 4-6
C. Bench Press, 4 x 4-6
D. Strict Pull Ups, 4-5 x Max Reps (1 RIR)
12779.notes:
Tomorrow we have a lifting complex of power clean + front squats + jerk, plus power cleans and biking.
You may superset your main lift with another DB/KB or bodyweight movement.
Pull-Ups: Use the following progression to guide you:
If you have…
> 10 unbroken reps: consider adding load.
5-10 unroken reps: perform as written.
< 5 unbroken reps: perform a cluster of sub-maximal reps for you with short rest between. For example: 3+2+2 or 2+1+1, with 15-20 sec of rest
0 body weight reps: perform 6-8 box pike or toe assisted reps per set, using as little lower body help as possible to achieve full ROM

12779.details:
3 Rounds for Quality/Load
A1. Alternating DB Bench Press, 3 x 12 (6 ea side)**
A2. Single Leg DB RDL, 3 x 6-8 ea
A3. L-Hang, 3 x 20-30 sec
**Athletes who performed barbell bench press for their strength work today can sub DB Lateral Raises or DB Lying Tricep Extensions, 3 x 12-15.
12779.notes:
Build in weight so your first set primes the movement patterns, and the latter two sets are hard and heavy. Rest 45-75 sec between movements.
L-Hang: Maintain active shoulders and toes above the hips. Accumulate time as needed, taking short rests between smaller “clusters” of the hold. If needed, scale back to a single leg hold or tuck hold.

12782.details:
Perform 6 sets of the complex for load:
1 Power Clean
1 Front Squat
1 Shoulder to Overhead
12782.notes: Rest as needed between your sets. Today you have the option of performing a press, push press or jerk to get the bar overhead. Compare to the complex we did on 7/14/25 (Week 2). The decrease in total volume should allow you to lift heavier across all of your work sets.

12782.details:
EMOM x 15 MIN
A: 3 Power Cleans
B: :20 Bike SPRINT
C: Rest
12782.notes:
We recommend fast, heavy singles on the power cleans rather than touch-and-go reps for this EMOM. Take the time to reset before each lift.
Advanced members should aim to lift around 75% or more of their 1RM. Beginners may need to reduce reps to maintain good form and cycle consistently from the floor.
On the bike, go for near red-line effort each round. Your performance will likely drop-off by rounds 4 or 5. Find a balance—push hard, but not so much that it compromises your power clean technique.

12783.notes:
This week, we’re building toward a challenging set of 3–5 reps across five work sets. You’ll likely need several warm up sets before getting started. This is one additional work set from last week.
If you’re confident in your sumo technique, reduce the reps and aim to lift heavier than in previous weeks.
If you’re still refining your form, stick with the higher rep range to get more practice at a moderately heavy load.

12783.details:
3-4 Rounds for Quality of:
10 Barbell Rollouts
8-12 Rear Delt Flyes with 1 count pause at the top of each rep
:30-60 Handstand Hold
12783.notes:
Complete 3–4 rounds, focusing on quality movement and control throughout.
Today is a great opportunity to get more comfortable being inverted. Your coach will offer progressions to help you work toward a more advanced handstand position.
Handstand Hold Options
Pike Handstand Hold (Feet on Box)
Inclined Handstand Hold (From Wall Walk)
Handstand Hold at Wall
Freestanding Handstand

12786.details:
3 Rounds For Time:
30 Push-Ups
30 Alternating Single DB Box Step Ups
800m Run
12786.notes:
Intent ~18-24 min. Today’s workout is straightforward, but not easy. Work with integrity on your push-ups, grind through the step ups, and find your own threshold of intensity on the run.
Push-Up Scaling: If you have…
> 10 reps unbroken, full volume is appropriate
5-10 reps unbroken, scale to 15-20 total reps per round
1-4 reps unbroken, scale to 5 reps from the floor + 15 elevated reps per round
0 bodyweight reps, scale to an elevation height that you cannot do more than 8-10 reps at a time with and do 20 reps per round.
Step Ups:
24/20/16″
+/50/35/20#/-
Scale as needed so you can stand all the way up on the leg that is leading the rep, rather than having to put your other foot down on the box to assist. Hold the DB either goblet, front rack, or behind-the-neck style.
Run: < 5 min
A. 550m
B. 4 Min Alternating Run/Walk, in 30-45 sec segments

12787.details:
Every 3 min x 5 Sets:
*Strict Pull-Ups, Chest to Bar Pull-Ups, or Ring Muscle-Ups
12787.notes:
Choose one movement and method to accumulate reps today.
Here are some suggestions, listed here from more advanced to more foundational:
A. Bodyweight, 4-5 sets x Max reps (1-2 RIR)
B. Accumulate Singles or Clusters in 90 sec
C. Accumulate 3-4 Negatives in 90 sec

12794.notes:
Use today’s assistance movements as a technique primer for your 3-Position Snatch complex.
We’re starting with a top-down segmented pull to groove the three snatch positions you’ll be working from today: high hang, below the knee, and floor. If you’re using an empty bar, pretend there are plates on the bar—stay tight and under tension when you pause at the “floor” (aka your start) position. Hold each pause for at least one count. When you stand up, hit each of those three positions again while smoothly pulling the bar to your hips.
The tall muscle snatch is a valuable drill for teaching and reinforcing the snatch turnover. It’s great for warming up that phase of the lift. An empty bar is usually best, though you can add weight if your goal is to strengthen the motion. Just remember—don’t sacrifice movement quality for load.
Beginner/Intermediate lifters: Start with a lighter barbell than you normally snatch to dial in tempo and precision.
Advanced lifters: Start with an empty bar, then either stay there or add a light load across rounds.

Compare to Week 1 (7/14/25). You may perform full or power snatches.
The 3-Position snatch complex consists of three consecutive snatches performed from different starting positions. This week’s sequence is: High hang → Below the knee → From the floor.
Pause briefly at the start of each rep to show control and balance with the barbell. This complex will also challenge your grip, so consider starting with lighter weights—around 60–75% of your 1RM—before increasing the load.

This benchmark workout features three bodyweight calisthentic movements and two barbell movements with very light weight. Expect it to burn 🔥 Scale barbell load and box height as needed so you can move with good mechanics throughout the workout.
CFSBK’s own Toni Smith has a logged score of 262 reps for this on BTWB!
Create a strategy to maximize your score while finding a pace that allows you to work at relatively high intensity for all three rounds. Scale barbell loading such that you could cycle 10+ reps at a time if desired.
Pull-Up Scaling
A. Chin Over Bar Pull-up (kipping or strict)
B. Foot Assisted Pull-up

12833.notes:
Accumulate a total of at least 12 quality reps on each side today, more if time allows. Trade arms as desired. Keep your eyes on the weight you’re using and use your core to stabilize your body throughout each rep. Take a beat to pause in each phase of the movement to create clear landmarks for yourself with this multi-part exercise.
Beginners: Use light to moderate loads throughout.
Int/Adv: Once you’ve established clear mechanics and consistency at light weights, build in load to something challenging for the day.

12833.details:
A. Back Squat, 5 x 1-3
B. Sumo Deadlift, 5 x 1-3
C. Bench Press, 5 x 1-3
D. Strict Pull Ups, 4-5 x Max Reps (1 RIR)
12833.notes:
Tomorrow we have a heavy single Front Squat, plus wall balls, rowing, and sandbag cleans.
If you’ve been consistent with one Floater Movement each week, feel confident with your technique, and have been feeling strong and well-recovered, consider building to a heavy single today. If you’ve missed sessions or want more technical practice, perform 5 sets of 1-3 heavy reps across.
You may superset your main lift with another DB/KB or bodyweight movement.
Pull-Ups: Use the following progression to guide you:
If you have…
> 10 unbroken reps: consider adding load.
5-10 unbroken reps: perform as written.
< 5 unbroken reps: perform a cluster of sub-maximal reps for you with short rest between. For example: 3+2+2 or 2+1+1, with 15-20 sec of rest
0 body weight reps: perform 6-8 box piked or toe assisted reps per set

12834.details:
Front Squat
Work up to a heavy single in 22 minutes.
12834.notes:
Today we are aiming to build confidence under heavy load, dial in bracing, and assess our current strength without maxing out recklessly. Heavy Single = A strong, challenging lift with good form. Not necessarily a lifetime PR. Stop before technique breaks down.
Start with 3-5 warm up sets sets of 3–5 reps. Once you’re at a challenging weight, drop to singles and aim for another 3-5 working sets. For example:
– – – Warm-Up Sets – – –
45 x 5
95 x 5
125 x 4
150 x 3
– – – Work Sets – – –
165 x 1
175 x 1
180 x 1
185 x 1
Remember: “Heavy” today depends on how you’re feeling. Quality movement > chasing numbers.

12834.details:
EMOM x 15 Min
A. 20 Wall Ball Shots
B. 15/12 Calories Row
C. 5 Sandbag Cleans
12834.notes:
Stimulus: This is a grindy, sustainable EMOM. Work should take ~40–45 seconds per station, leaving a little recovery and transition time before the next minute.
Wall Ball: It’s a good day to get out of your comfort zone here! Increase the weight of your ball or/and the height of your target to test your accuracy, without compromising mechanics.
Row: Target a consistent pace (not a sprint). Think “strong pulls, steady recovery.”
Sandbag Cleans: Lap the bag first, then hug it and drive tall. Use your hips, not your arms, and keep the bag close. Stay braced, breathe between reps, and aim for smooth sets of 5.

12835.details:
3-4 Rounds for Quality
16-20 Russian Twists
15-20 Banded Face Pulls
5-8ea Deficit Single Leg Calf Raise

Complete as many rounds as possible in 20 minutes of:
400m Run
Max Strict Pull-ups
12835.notes:
In this 20-minute AMRAP you’ll run 400 meters, then go straight into a max set of strict pull-ups. Remember, strict doesn’t mean slow, stay tight (hollow shape); drive your elbows down, and pull your chin quickly over the bar. Use the run as your recovery so you can keep hitting quality pull-ups each round. Most athletes should aim for five to six total rounds.
Scaling:
If you have strict pull-ups but are unable to perform at least 5 reps, begin each set with a max set of strict pull-ups, then stay on the bar for a max set of kipping pull-ups. If you do not yet have strict pull-ups, perform a moderately challenging version of banded strict pull-ups or ring rows.
In case of injury or limitation, perform 800/1,000 meters on a bike or 400/500 meters on a rower. For the strict pull-ups, if hanging is not an option for you, you can perform dumbbell bent-over rows.
Scaling option A:
400m Run
Max-rep strict pull-ups + kipping pull-ups
Scaling option B:
400m Run
Max-rep banded strict pull-ups

12836.details:
A1. 3×6-8 Barbell Romanian Deadlifts @ Tempo 3111
A2. 3x10ea DB or KB Goblet Reverse Lunges
12836.notes:
After 1-2 lighter warm up sets on the barbell, perform the two movements as a superset, resting about 60-90 sec between each.
Complete all the lunges on one side before changing to the other side.
In this first week of the cycle, focus on quality reps with as close to perfect mechanics as you can achieve and holding the tempo for the RDLs. Use a regular grip or hook grip; no switch grip today.

12836.details:
“Half Flight Simulator”
For Time
10-20-30-40-50-40-30-20-10
Unbroken Double Unders
Time Cap: 10 min
12836.notes:
With a running clock, perform 10 unbroken Double-Unders. Stop. Perform 20 unbroken Double-Unders. Stop. Perform 30 Double-Unders, etc. Continue with this pattern, increasing by 10 until the set of 50 unbroken Double-Unders, then back down to 10.
Each set must be unbroken. The rope must stop moving before starting the next set. Rest as needed between sets. A failed Double-Under (either because the rope stops or because the rope passes under the feet only once) counts as a broken set. If a set is broken, start again from the beginning of that set.
Today’s workout involves 250 total repetitions. Choose a scaling option below that challenges your skill while allowing you to finish in under 8 minutes. Advanced athletes should target completing this under 4 minutes.
A. 5-10-15-20-25-20-15-10-5 (125 reps)
B. Complete 10 Sets of 10 Unbroken Reps for Time (100 reps)
C. Accumulate 50 total Double Unders or Attempts (count your misses as well as your makes)
D. 15-30-45-60-75-60-45-30-15 Unbroken Single Unders

12841.notes:
Our goal here is to accumulate some volume with technically sound, crisp reps and establish a baseline of good mechanics with the rack position, vertical dip, and leg drive.
Today, reset at the rack position for each rep, rather than cycling or linking the reps together through the dip.
If you have a recent or well-established 1 rep max, use ~70% of that for your work sets. If not, go by rate of perceived exertion and work in the realm of 6-7 for how you’re feeling today.
Either way, this will be moderate load and you should have multiple good reps in the tank left on each set. Ideally we get 4 working sets at the same weight, but a little wiggle room is fine here for today.

12841.details:
12 Rounds For Time (6 ea)
3 Wall Walks
12/9 Cal Row
12841.notes:
Intent: 11-15 min
Breathe steadily during your time inverted and create as much leg drive on the erg as possible!
Wall Walk Scaling
A. 2 Full ROM reps (hands ~6″ from wall)
B. 2-3 Partial ROM Reps
C. 30 sec Angled Hollow Body Inversion Hold

12842.details:
A. Front Squat, Heavy Single
B. Romanian Deadlift, 3 x 6-8 @ 3111 tempo
C. Push Press, 4 x 5 @ 70% / RPE 6-7
D. Weighted Chin-Up, Heavy Single
12842.notes:
Tomorrow we have ring muscle ups and snatches.
The front squat is intended as a heavy, quality rep, not an all out 1 rep max test. Build some confidence under challenging load, but call it before form breaks down.
You may superset your main lift with another DB/KB or bodyweight movement.
Chin-Up Progression: Choose something difficult for you that allows for consistent mechanics and full ranges of motion.
A. Work up to a heavy single (in about 6-8 total sets)
B. Perform 4-5 Sets x 1-3 Reps or Negatives at bodyweight
C. Perform 4-5 Sets x 5 Reps of Box Pike or Foot Assisted Chin-Ups

12842.details:
For Time
50/40 Cal Bike
-then-
3 Rounds of:
15 Russian KB Swings 24/16kg
10 Burpee Box Jump Overs 24/20″
12842.notes:
Intent ~7-12 min
Bike: < 5 min
KB: Light and snappy today! Advanced athletes can experiment with a “power swing” today to increase their cycle rate.
BBJO:
Athletes must step down on the opposite side of their box but do not need to achieve hip or knee extension atop the box.
Scale to a lower box and/or by stepping up and over the box. If stepping up, both feet must touch the top of the box before moving to the other side.

12837.details:
9-7-5 Reps for time of:
Bar Muscle-ups
Squat Snatches, 135/95 lbs
Time cap: 10 min
12837.notes:
With two high-skill movements, this one requires a bit of “riding the edge.” If you fail a rep, make the adjustments needed and try again. If you fail two reps in a row, employ scaling options by reducing load or movement complexity.
Muscle Up Scaling: Choose a difficult variation that challenges your skill and strength.
A. 7-5-3
B. 5-4-3
D. 9-7-5 reps of “Pull+Push” … Here are 3 different examples of what Round 1 could look like:
Ex: 9 Strict CTB Pull-Ups + 9 Ring Dips
OR
Ex: 9 Strict Pull-Ups + 9 Matador Dips
OR
Ex: 9 Strict Banded Pull-ups + 9 Bench Dips
Snatch: Moderately heavy, in the realm of 65-75%. These are full snatches, passing through a below-parallel squat on each rep! Most athletes will be doing quick singles to get through the 21 reps.

12843.details:
A. Front Squat, Heavy Single
B. Romanian Deadlift, 3 x 6-8 @ 3111 tempo
C. Push Press, 4 x 5 @ 70% / RPE 7
D. Weighted Chin-Up, Heavy Single
12843.notes:
Tomorrow we have front squats, wall ball shots, air squats, and box jump overs.
The front squat is intended as a heavy, quality rep, not an all out 1 rep max test. Build some confidence under challenging load, but call it before form breaks down.
You may superset your main lift with another DB/KB or bodyweight movement.
Chin-Up Progression: Choose something difficult for you that allows for consistent mechanics and full ranges of motion.
A. Work up to a heavy single (in about 6-8 total sets)
B. Perform 4-5 Sets x 1-3 Reps or Negatives at bodyweight
C. Perform 4-5 Sets x 5 Reps of Box Pike or Foot Assisted Chin-Ups

12843.details:
EMOM x 15 MIN
A. 40 sec Max Reps Shuttle Runs (40 feet)
B. 40 sec Farmers March
C. 40 sec Max Reps Straight Leg Sit-Ups OR Toes to Bar
12843.notes:
Shuttle Runs: One “rep” = 40 feet (2×20′ lengths, or down and back)
March: Use two heavy KBs that challenge your grip. Stand tall and stay balanced as you march steadily in place. If you are not coming to class tomorrow and want to challenge your upper back strength instead, perform a dual KB front rack march.
Sit-ups: Each rep starts with the fingertips touching the floor overhead and finishes with fingertips touching the toes. If needed, scale to touch as far forward as your mobility allows. Athletes with strict or kipping toes to bar can elect to do that movement today (but not recommended if you came to class yesterday).

12846.notes:
Our goal today is to accumulate some volume with technically sound, crisp reps and establish a baseline of good mechanics with the front rack position, vertical torso, and speed out of the hole.
If you were here for the heavy single, use about 65% up to 70% of your best rep. If you did not come last Monday, work at a load that feels like RPE 5 to 6.
Either way, this will be moderate load and you should have multiple good reps in the tank left on each set.

12846.details:
3 Rounds for Time
16 Alternating DB Hang Power Snatches
30 Air Squats
12 Box Jump Overs (24/20″)
Intent: 6-10min
12846.notes:
The workout is designed to be short and punchy. Push the pace but don’t blow up in Round 1. Find a sustainable speed in the air squats and then attack the snatches and box jumps. Aim to keep each round under 3 minutes to hit the intended stimulus.
DB: Choose a weight you can cycle confidently and complete unbroken or in two quick sets max.
Move smoothly through the air squats, don’t rush and lose depth, but keep a steady rhythm.
The box jump overs are where heart rate will spike, so stay efficient with footwork and step down if needed to keep moving safely. Scale height of the box as low as needed today!

12848.notes:
Today is all about building confidence and control upside down. Use the time to practice smooth kick-ups and strong, active handstand holds. Keep the focus on technique and body position.
When kicking up, start small and controlled, then build height as you feel more confident. Think about stacking your hips over your shoulders and pressing the floor away with strong, active arms. Don’t rush, find balance with tight legs and a strong core.
For the handstand holds, aim for short sets of 10–20 seconds where you can stay in a good hollow body position. Quality holds will help you build strength and balance faster than maxing out until you fall.
Practice safe bail-outs. If you feel yourself tipping over, turn your body into a cartwheel rather than crashing down.

12850.details:
A1. Barbell Good Mornings, 4×6-8
A2. Rear Foot Elevated Split Squats, 4×6-8ea
12850.notes:
After 1-2 warm up sets with the barbell, perform the two movements as a superset, resting about 60-90 sec between each.
Use a slower-down, faster-up tempo on both exercises.
Good Mornings: Maintain a braced, rigid trunk and perform the movement by flexing and extending at the hips. Focus your attention on stretching and loading into the glutes and hamstrings on the descent of each rep.
Split Squats: Hold 1 or 2 DB’s suitcase style. If balance is a challenge for you, grab a pvc pipe to hold/push into the ground to assist you. Complete all reps on one side before changing to the other side.

12850.details:
For Time
10 Power Cleans @ 155/105#
400m Run
20 Power Cleans
800m Run
12850.notes:
Intent: 8-13 min
Load is on the heavier side of moderate, in the realm of 60-70%. Scale to a weight you are comfortable completing quick singles with and could cycle a few unbroken reps if required.
If your 800m / half mile run pace is greater than 5 minutes, consider scaling one or both runs back slightly:
A. 270m (4th Ave and back) / 680m (full lap + 3rd Ave and back)
B. 200m (mural and back) / 550m (full lap)
If you are building tolerance to running, use a mixed approach in each round:
130m Run + 400m Bike / 270m Run + 800m Bike

12852.details:
Push Press
5 sets x 3 reps @ 75%-80% or RPE 7
12852.notes:
This is our second and final week with push press before we progress to the push jerk. Dial in your rack position, dip, and leg drive today — all of that will carry over to the rest of the cycle!
If you have a recent or well-established 1 rep max, use ~75-80% of that for your work sets. If not, work at about RPE 7 for how you feel today.
Either way, this should be heavier than last week, and you should still have a couple reps in the tank on each set.

12852.details:
3-5 Rounds for Load and Quality
10 ea Single Arm DB Chainsaw Row
40 sec Dual KB Front Rack March
5-10 Strict Toes to Bar @ 2 sec down tempo
1:00 Bike @ recovery pace
12852.notes:
Start with moderate loads for the first two movements and work up in weight as long as you are able to maintain consistent mechanics.
Toes to Bar: Hold the tempo! Control throughout. No swing, no kip. Minimize lat pushdown in this variation. Scale the movement to Incline Strict TTB i if needed so you can work on active compression through the abs and hip flexors to bring the legs to the torso.

12853.details:
A. Front Squat, 4×5 @ 65-70%
B. Rear Foot Elevated Split Squat, 4 x 6-8
C. Push Press, 5×3 @ 75-80%
D. Weighted Matador Dip, 3-3-3-3
12853.notes:
Tomorrow we have pull-ups and thrusters.
You may superset your main lift with another DB/KB or bodyweight movement.
Squat: If you don’t have a good feel for percentages yet, work to RPE 5-6 for 4 sets of 5 reps across. You should have multiple good reps in the tank on each set.
Dips: If you missed Tuesday’s workout and have the ability, find a heavy 3 weighted strict dip. You could also work on bodyweight, banded, or foot assisted reps.

12853.details:
3 Intervals of
3 Min Row for Max Meters
Rest 3 min between Intervals
12853.notes:
While simple, this workout will be potent if approached correctly. Focus first and foremost on your technique, not just your effort.
Aim to work at what feels like 85% of your aerobic threshold on the first interval. Another way to guide yourself is by picking a pace you think you could actually hold for closer to 5-6 minutes straight if you needed to.
On interval two, sustain that pace with the goal of achieving a similar meters “score.” On interval three, push a little harder and see if you can squeeze out a bit more!

12855.details:
9-15-21 Reps for Time of:
Pull-Ups
Thrusters (95/65#)
12855.notes:
This workout is a familiar couplet known as “Fran,” but today we’ll flip it and reverse it! Both the rep sceme and the movement order is reversed.
The intent for today is a quick burn. Fast Fran times are under 4 minutes and today should be under 9! Scale as needed to get a true dose of intensity today.
Pull-Up Scaling:
A. 9-12-15 Kipping
B. 6-8-10 Strict
C. 6-8-10 Foot or Band Assisted Strict
D. Jumping Pull-Ups (full volume)
Thruster: Light weight that you could complete 15+ reps with unbroken.

12858.details:
A. Front Squat, 4×5 @ 65-70%
B. Rear Foot Elevated Split Squat, 4 x 6-8
C. Push Press, 5×3 @ 75-80%
D. Weighted Matador Dip, 3-3-3-3
12858.notes:
Tomorrow we have Front Squats and assistance work.
You may superset your main lift with another DB/KB or bodyweight movement.
Squat: If you don’t have a good feel for percentages yet, work to RPE 5-6 for 4 sets of 5 reps across. You should have multiple good reps in the tank on each set.
Dips: If you missed Tuesday’s workout and have the ability, find a heavy 3 weighted strict dip. You could also work on bodyweight, banded, or foot assisted reps.

12858.details:
For Time:
200 Double Unders
50 Burpees
50 Cal Bike
Time Cap: 14 min
12858.notes:
Today’s workout is a chipper. Start by completing all 200 reps with the jump rope before moving on to the 50 burpees and finally to the bike. A good amount of mental fortitude will be required to get your best time on this workout. Focus on the rep in front of you and keep working hard, even and especially when it gets challenging.
No individual element here should take longer than 5 minutes. Scale one, two, or all three of the movements to finish your version under the time cap.
DU: Reduce volume and/or plan to practice for 4 minutes and count as many attempts and makes as you get!
Burpees:
A. 25 full ROM reps + 25 no push-up reps
B. 15 full ROM reps + 35 no push-up reps
C. 50 no-push up reps

12859.notes: This is a volume strength session focused on reinforcing front rack position, bracing, and consistent squat mechanics. The load should feel moderate, challenging but never near failure. RPE 6–7 means athletes finish each set with about 3 reps left in the tank.

12859.details:
3-4 Rounds for Quality
:30/:30 Copenhagen Plank
1:00 Crossover Single Unders
16 Alternating Tall Kneeling Rotational Med Ball Slam, 8ea
1:00 Arch Hold
12859.notes:
This is accessory work meant to build core strength, stability, and durability, move with control and focus on quality, not speed or max effort.
For the Copenhagen plank, keep your hips high and body in a straight line; the focus is on adductor (inner thigh) strength, so pick a knee or foot position you can hold with good form.
During crossovers, stay light on your feet, find rhythm, and work coordination rather than going all out.
On the medball slams the intention is to focus on rotational core strength, so make sure you are bracing before slamming the ball to the floor.
Finally, in the arch hold, squeeze glutes, keep arms and legs off the ground, and focus on holding a strong, tight shape. Treat this as practice, consistent, high-quality movement and it will pay off in bigger lifts and gymnastics skills later on.

12861.details:
AMRAP 30 MIN
700m Row or 1400m Bike
12 Strict Chin-Ups
21 Tuck-Ups
500m Row or 1000m Bike
9 Strict Chin-Ups
15 Tuck-Ups
300m Row or 600m Bike
6 Strict Chin-Ups
9 Tuck-Ups
*After each full round of work, switch which machine you use. Large classes will be paired up so one person does a full round on the bike while the other does a full round on the erg, and then swap.
12861.notes:
Intent: 2-3 rounds.
This is a long, steady grind with a focus on strict pulling strength and midline endurance. The intent is 2–3 full rounds in 30 minutes, so pace accordingly. Smooth on the machines, steady on the gymnastics.
On the row/bike, think moderate effort, not sprint. Each machine segment should leave you breathing but ready to go straight into the pull-ups.
For the strict chin-ups, break early to avoid failure; small sets with short rests will keep you moving better than big sets to burnout. Scale by using band or foot/box-assistance that provides challenge while allowing for full range of motion on each rep.
On the tuck-ups, stay controlled and keep your lower back pressed to the floor at the bottom of the rep.
Because you switch machines each round, approach this like an endurance piece, find a rhythm you can maintain the whole 30 minutes. Consistency and smart pacing are the keys to hitting the stimulus.

12864.details:
A1. 4×5 Conventional Deadlift @ RPE 7-7.5
A2. 4×20 sec ea Split Squat Pallof Press
12864.notes:
Take 3-4 warm-up sets to find a moderately heavy load (RPE 7-7.5) for 5 reps on the deadlift, then complete 4 work sets across. You should have 2-3 reps in reserve at this weight.
Once at work weight, superset the deadlifts with the pallof press. Maintain a stable position with the back knee hovering just a few inches off the floor as you extend the arms and bring them back into the body.

12864.details:
3 Intervals, Each for Time
550m Run
Rest 1:1
12864.notes:
If you’ve got a buddy in class that runs around your same pace, see if you can inspire a bit of friendly competition today to light a fire and keep you focused. Start your first interval around RPE 8 — vigorous effort, but with a bit left in the tank. Then, challenge each other to see if you can hold pace or get a little bit faster on the next two runs.
Scale to a run distance you can complete in under 3:30.

12865.details:
Push Jerk
5 sets x 3 reps @ 70%-75% or RPE 6-7
12865.notes:
If you have a recent or well-established 1 rep max push jerk, use ~70-75% of that for your work sets. If not, work at about RPE 6-7 for how you feel today. We’re aiming for crisp reps: powerful leg drive, clear timing, accurate footwork, and no press-outs!
We worked a lot on the jerk rack position, dip, and leg drive in the past two weeks. Do your best to incorporate what you practiced into this more dynamic movement.
If you struggle with wrist pain or other discomfort on these lifts, make sure you’re properly re-racking the bar from overhead and getting back to your best possible position each time with the shoulders and trunk supporting the bar, not your hands and arms.

12865.details:
4 Rounds, for Max Load
5 Hang Power Cleans
5 Push Press
10 Alternating Reverse Lunges, 5ea
15-20 sec Barbell Overhead Hold
Rest as needed between rounds.
12865.notes:
Complete the four movements as one unbroken set. Find the heaviest load you can use with consistent mechanics. Though labeled as assistance work, this will certainly get the heartrate up a bit!
For the lunges, a front rack or back rack hold may be used.
After the lunges, any method of getting the barbell back overhead is allowed (push press, push jerk, split jerk). Hold with straight arms and strong midline stabilization for 15-20 seconds.

12866.details:
A. Front Squat, 5×4 @ 70-75%
B. Deadlift, 4×5 @ RPE 7-7.5
C. Push Jerk, 5×3 @ 70-75%
D. Strict Chin Ups, 4×8-10
12866.notes:
Tomorrow we have rowing, push ups, deadlifts, biking, toes to bar, and DB front squats!
You may superset your main lift with another DB/KB or bodyweight movement.
Squat: If you don’t have a good feel for percentages yet, work to RPE 6-7 for 5 sets of 4 reps across.
Deadlift: Aim for a weight that leaves you 2-3 reps in reserve. We have deadlifts in tomorrow’s workout, so choosing this is not advised if you’re attending tmw!
Chin Ups: If you cannot complete 8-10 unbroken reps, accumulate that volume with one of the following strategies…
A. 4 sets x [Max bodyweight reps + foot assisted reps to finish out 8-10 total per set]
B. 2-3 sets x [10 sec lock off + 10 sec negative], followed by 2-3 sets x 8-10 foot assisted reps

12866.details:
For Time
50-40-30-20-10 Double Unders
*40′ Sandbag Bearhug Carry after each set
12866.notes:
In this workout, Partner A completes 50 DU’s, then a 40′ carry. Then Partner B completes 50 DU’s and a 40′ carry. On the next round, Partner A does 40 DU’s, and the carry remains the same distance. Continue in this fashion until each partner has finished their round of 10 DU’s + 40′ carry.
Intent <12 min.
DU Scaling
A. 40-30-20-10-5
B. 25-20-15-10-5
C. 5-10 DU attempts each round + 50-40-30-20-10 single unders.
Sandbag: 40 feet = “down and back” across the 20ft tape lines in the gym. This is a short distance so choose a heavy bag to carry!

12867.details:
🎉 CFSBK’S 18TH BIRTHDAY WORKOUT FUN TIMES EXCELLENT AMAZING GOOD JOB! 🎉
AMRAP 18 MIN
18 Cal Row
18 Push-ups
18 Deadlifts (185/125#)
18 Cal Bike
18 Toes to Bar
18 DB Front Squats (50/35#)
12867.notes:
Today we celebrate CFSBK’s 18th Anniversary… 18 years of fitness, fun, and foolishness 🤪
This workout is about steady pacing and managing fatigue across multiple movement patterns. Eighteen minutes is long enough that you should avoid redlining early. Aim to finish at least 2 rounds of work, scaling accordingly.
Push-Ups: break them up early if needed to keep form tight. Scale volume or to elevated reps.
DL: moderate load; think quick sets of 6–9 reps rather than all 18 unbroken.
TTB: prioritize good kip rhythm and small, smart sets before grip blows up. Scale to hanging leg or knee raises.
DB FSQ: Keep elbows high, chest tall, and drive through the legs. These will get spicy when paired with the hinge and core work. Scale to a weight you can complete 6-9 reps at a time with.
Remember why you love this place, cheer on your fellow athletes, and have fun!

12870.details:
A. Front Squat, 5×4 @ 70-75%
B. Deadlift, 4×5 @ RPE 7-7.5
C. Push Jerk, 5×3 @ 70-75%
D. Strict Chin Ups, 4×8-10
12870.notes:
Tomorrow we have front squats, running, crawling, and sandbag cleans!
You may superset your main lift with another DB/KB or bodyweight movement.
Squat and Push Jerk: If you don’t have a good feel for percentages yet, work to RPE 6-7 for 5 sets.
Deadlift: Aim for a weight that leaves you 2-3 reps in reserve.
Chin-Ups: If you cannot complete 8-10 unbroken reps, accumulate that volume with one of the following strategies…
A. 4 sets x [Max bodyweight reps + Foot assisted reps to finish out 8-10 total per set]
B. 2-3 sets x [10 sec lock off + 10 sec negative], followed by 2-3 sets x 8-10 foot assisted reps

12870.details:
3 Rounds for Time
15 Hang Power Snatches (75/55#)
400m Run
12870.notes:
Intent <12 min
Snatch: Choose a light load you can complete in 1-3 sets each time. The hang position can be anywhere above the knee today. Always stand up fully to complete the rep before bringing the bar back down to the hang.
Since we are working with light loads, do not bail the bar from overhead today! It destroys the 10 and 15# plates. Control the bar to your hip and then set it down. If you want to bail at the 75lb load, use a 15lb bar + 25lb plates and 5’s on the outside.
Run: Go a little faster than you want to! Scale back to 270m if the full effort will take longer than 2:30.

12871.notes: At 75% to 80%, or around RPE 7 to 8, we’re now at moderate-to-heavy load. The weight should feel challenging but not like a true max. Focus on keeping your elbows high, chest tall, and core braced throughout every rep. Each set should feel heavy but repeatable, leaving one to two reps in the tank.

12871.details:
“The Predator”
800m Run
200′ Crawl
4 Sandbag Cleans
400m Run
160′ Crawl
8 Sandbag Cleans
200m Run
120′ Crawl
12 Sandbag Cleans
12871.notes:
Intent 15-20 min.
Workout courtesy of Coach Cara! A little note from her: “The Predator is a workout model inspired by wolves and other distance predators who have to track and follow their prey for long distances, get close enough to strike, tussle with their prey, then repeat the cycle until they’re able to finish the kill.”
This workout is about grit. The runs get shorter each round, but the crawls and sandbag cleans will feel longer and heavier, so it is important to be stubborn towards the end.
Run: Settle into a controlled pace that allows you to attack the crawl without redlining.
Crawl: Move steadily, and avoid rushing to save your shoulders and core.
Sandbag Cleans: Choose a heavy bag! Brace your core, use your hips; and drive through the floor. Break them into quick singles if needed, but stay close to the bag and reset right away.

12872.details:
3-4 Rounds For Quality
1:00 Handstand Hold
12-15 Seated Reverse Flies
:30 Sec Hanging L-Sit Hold
1:00 Crossover Single Unders
12872.notes:
This accessory work is designed to build stability, shoulder health, and midline strength while sneaking in some light aerobic movement. The intent is three to four steady rounds where you prioritize strong positions and controlled effort so you finish feeling stronger, not burned out.
HS Hold: Focus on pressing tall through the shoulders, keeping your core tight, and maintaining a hollow body position. Accumulate 1:00 per round, taking breaks as needed. Scale to angled wall-facing hollow inversion hold or box pike hold.
Reverse Flies: Should be done with light weights, moving slowly and squeezing the shoulder blades together on every rep to strengthen the upper back.
L-sit hold: Keep your legs as straight as possible, press down firmly through your arms, and brace your core to hold a tight position for the full thirty seconds with the toes above the hips. Scale by bending one knee or both knees into the chest for a tuck variation. Accumulate time if needed.
Crossover single unders: Play with the skill! Use this as a chance to keep moving while staying relaxed.

12872.details:
EMOM x 10 MIN
5 Burpees
10 Push ups
12872.notes:
This looks simple, but it will be humbling for many of us!
Scale the workout so you can complete your first few rounds in under 35 seconds or so. This will likely stretch out as the workout continues. Be prepared to break your push-ups up and “chip away” with small sets. Keep the integrity of your movement. Hold the standard and complete 150 reps where your chest touches the ground!
Scaling
A. 5 Burpees + 5-7 Push-Ups
B. 3 Burpees + 10 Incline Push-Ups

12873.details:
A1. 3×6-8 Barbell Romanian Deadlifts @ Tempo 3111
A2. 3x8ea Goblet Box Step ups
12873.notes:
After 2-3 warm up sets on the barbell, perform the two movements as a superset, resting about a minute between each.
RDL: This is the same rep/tempo scheme as Week 1. Aim to go a bit heavier. Use a regular grip or hook grip for as long as possible.
Step Up: Choose a box that puts your thigh relatively parallel to the floor, rather than a higher box and “below parallel” depth. Challenge yourself on the loading at this mid-range. Minimize push off from the bottom leg as much as possible. Complete all the reps on one side before changing to the other side. You may keep your foot on the box throughout the set or take it off and step it back up, athlete’s choice.

12873.details:
5 Intervals of
In 1:30
6 Horizontal Ring Rows
12 Box Jumps (24/20″)
Max Calorie Bike
Rest 1:30
12873.notes:
Intent is to have at least 30 seconds on the bike each round. Scale one or both of the first movements as needed to achieve that consistently.
Ring Rows: RX’d version is feet on bench with body completely parallel to floor in start position. Maintain solid plank position throughout and resist the urge to kip the movement or use momentum as fatigue accumulates. Scale by placing feet on the floor and choosing a very difficult angle for 6 unbroken reps, possibly breaking into two quick sets in later rounds.
Box Jump: Scale height of the box as needed to jump today. Fully extend the legs and hips at the top of each rep. Work on cycling reps efficiently: pause briefly at the top to get balanced and stable. Step one foot down, and as the second foot touches the floor jump immediately back to the box. The place to rest or re-group is at the top of the box, not the floor.

12874.details:
Push Jerk
5 sets x 2 reps @ 75-80% or RPE 7-8
12874.notes:
If you have a recent or well-established 1 rep max push jerk, use ~75-80% of that for your work sets. If not, work at about RPE 7-8 for how you feel today. We’re aiming for crisp reps: powerful leg drive, clear timing, accurate footwork, and no press-outs!
On that note: Locking out a lift requires you establish the overhead position forcefully before the full weight of the bar is pushing down on you. It has to be proactive as part of a continuous, committed motion—you can’t wait to feel the weight and then react to it. Make it a focus on every lift to never let up on pushing up against the bar, and to lock in your shoulder blades forcefully for a solid base to prevent bouncing. Reach and punch up!

12874.details:
12 Rounds for Time (6ea)
8 Toes to Bar
4 Hang Power Snatches
8 Overhead Squats
12874.notes:
Partners alternate full rounds of work. Intent ~10-15 min.
TTB: To be completed in 1-2 sets consistently. Scale volume or range of motion as needed.
A. 4-6 Kipping TTB
B. 4 Strict TTB
C. 8 Kipping Leg Raise, toes as high as possible
D. 8 V-Ups
Barbell: 95/65/45#. Light load. Use the same weight for both exercises. Ideally, complete the 12 reps as an unbroken set. Hang position can be anywhere above the knee.

12876.details:
A. Front Squat, 5×3 @ 75-80% (RPE 7-8)
B. Romanian Deadlift, 3×6-8 @ 3111 Tempo
C. Push Jerk, 5×2 @ 75-80% (RPE 7-8)
D. Weighted Chin-ups, 2-2-2-2-2
12876.notes:
Tomorrow we have DB Snatches, Lunges and Burpees
You may superset your main lift with another DB/KB or bodyweight movement.
Squat and Push Jerk: If you don’t have a good feel for percentages yet, work to RPE 7-8 for 5 sets across.
RDL: If you did this in Week 1, aim to go heavier while maintaining tempo and technique.
Chin-Up Progression: Do a couple of warm up sets (foot assisted ring pull-ups, negatives, lock offs, etc.). Then choose something difficult for you that allows for consistent mechanics and full ranges of motion.
A. 5 Sets x 2 weighted Chin-Ups, building to find a heavy double
B. 5 Sets x 1-3 bodyweight Chin-Ups or Negatives
C. 5 Sets x 5 tough reps of Box Pike or Foot Assisted Chin-Ups

Intent ~9-15 min
This is a CF benchmark workout, cut down in half for a smaller, but potent dose! Each individual element should be under 5 minutes. Scale volume of one or both movements as needed to preserve the stimulus of the workout and keep intensity high. Examples below, mix and match as needed:
Scaling Option A
680m Run
800m Row
680m Run
Scaling Option B
550m Run
700m Row
550m Run

12877.details:
2 Rounds for Time
50 Alternating DB Snatches, 25ea (50/35#)
40 Alternating DB Reverse Lunges, 20ea
30 Lateral Burpees over the DB
12877.notes:
Intent ~ 12-18 min
Today’s workout contains two rounds with higher repetitions of each movement. With higher reps, manage your pace and move to rest minimally during your breaks. Athletes who want a challenge should go unbroken on the snatches and go right into the lunges. If you choose this route, buckle up and enjoy the ride.
For the dumbbell lunges, carry the dumbbell however you like.
DB Snatches: Keep your back flat, drive through the legs, and switch smoothly overhead. Sets of 10–15 reps at a time are manageable for most.
Lunges: Step back under control, keep your torso upright, and touch the knee lightly without slamming down.
Burpees: will spike your heart rate, focus on steady rhythm rather than sprinting early.
Scaling option A:
2 rounds for time:
50 Alt. DB Snatches 35/20
40 DB Reverse Lunges
30 Lateral Burpees over the DB
Scaling option B:
2 rounds for time:
20 Alt. DB Snatches 20/10
20 DB Reverse Lunges
20 Lateral Burpees over the DB

12877.details:
2-3 Rounds
12-15 DB Bicep curls
12-15 DB Tricep extensions

12879.details:
A. Front Squat, 5×3 @ 75-80% (RPE 7-8)
B. Romanian Deadlift, 3×6-8 @ 3111 Tempo
C. Push Jerk, 5×2 @ 75-80% (RPE 7-8)
D. Weighted Chin-ups, 2-2-2-2-2
12879.notes:
Tomorrow we have front squats and assistance work including DB bench press.
You may superset your main lift with another DB/KB or bodyweight movement.
Squat and Push Jerk: If you don’t have a good feel for percentages yet, work to RPE 7-8 for 5 sets across.
RDL: If you did this in Week 1, aim to go heavier while maintaining tempo and technique.
Chin-Up Progression: Do a couple of warm up sets (foot assisted ring pull-ups, negatives, lock offs, etc.). Then choose something difficult for you that allows for consistent mechanics and full ranges of motion.
A. 5 Sets x 2 weighted Chin-Ups, building to find a heavy double
B. 5 Sets x 1-3 bodyweight Chin-Ups or Negatives
C. 5 Sets x 5 tough reps of Box Pike or Foot Assisted Chin-Ups

12879.details:
4 Rounds for Time
65 Double Unders
65m Single Arm Farmer Carry, ea (24/16kg)
12879.notes:
Intent ~12-16min
DU’s < 1:30/round
A. 25-50 reps
B. 5-10 attempts + 65 single unders
Carry: Moderate load that you can complete unbroken and keep great body position with. Carry down to 3rd Ave on one hand and back on the other. Whichever hand you finish with will be a bit more taxed before re-starting the jump rope!

12880.details:
Front Squat
6 Sets x 2 Reps @ 80% – 85% / RPE 7-8
12880.notes:
Heavy doubles today! Focus on bracing, staying tight, and moving with speed out of the hole. Each set should feel challenging but never sloppy, quality over load.
Rest 2–3 minutes between sets to keep lifts strong and consistent.

12880.details:
3-5 Rounds for Quality and Load
8-12 DB Bench Press
6 Tall Box Jumps
15-20 Candlestick toe touches
12 Paused Wall Ball Shots
12880.notes:
Focus on quality over speed in every movement.
DB Bench press: Pick a weight you can control for smooth, stable reps.
Box Jumps: Use a low, soft box and focus on vertical extension today. Fully extend your knees and hips in the air, and aim to land as “tall” as possible on the box.
Candlestick toe touches: Engage your core and avoid using momentum.
Paused Wall Ball Shots: Hold at the bottom for 1 full second on tension, stay tall, then drive up with power. Up for a challenge? Grab a heavier medicine ball today and get out of your comfort zone!

12881.details:
EMOM x 32 Min
A. 6 Shuttle Runs (40′)
B. 8-12 Kipping Pull-Ups*
C. 12/9 Cal Bike -or- 15/12 Cal Row
D. 40 sec Ring Plank
12881.notes:
With 8 rounds of work and no rest minute, many athletes will need to scale this workout to make the output sustainable. Remove ego and set yourself up for success today.
The main training goal here is to work efficient kipping pull-up technique. If you’re building mechanics and consistency with this, break your reps in to smart sets right away. If you start to lose range of motion or form degrades, reduce volume of reps per minute. If you are already technically proficient, push for bigger unbroken sets.
Your first two rounds should be a manageable amount of work to complete in ~40 seconds per minute. As you fatigue, effort will need to increase and that time may stretch a bit.
Shuttle Run: Each rep is “down and back” across the tape lines, 40 feet. Complete 6 “down and backs” for a total of 240 feet. If you prefer, just count each time you turn around and count to 12! Touch both feet and 1 hand down on the far side of the line on each turnaround.
*Pull-Ups:
RX+ 4-6 Bar Muscle Ups or 8-12 Chest-to-bar Pull-Ups
A. 8-12 Kipping
B. 4-6 Strict (bodyweight)
C. 6-10 Foot or Band Assisted Strict

12882.details:
For Load and Max Wattage:
21 Deadlifts (315/205#)
15 sec Max Wattage Bike
Rest 3 Minutes
15 Deadlifts
15 sec Max Wattage Bike
Rest 3 Minutes
9 Deadlifts
15 sec Max Wattage Bike
12882.notes:
This workout is short, heavy, and explosive. Every set should feel like a sprint.
Deadlifts: Heavy enough to demand respect, but should still allow for quick singles or small touch-and-go sets. Maintain a flat back and tight brace every rep.
Bike: Goal is all-out wattage for just 15 seconds. Empty the tank, then rely on the rest period to recover before the next round.
Use the 3 minutes of rest wisely. Walk around, shake out your legs, and be ready to hit the next effort at 100%.
Expect it to feel like a max effort sprint repeat workout: heavy pull into pure power output.
Scaling
Deadlifts: Drop load to something that allows crisp, heavy sets of 1-5 reps.
Bike: Focus on a hard sprint or RPE 9-10 effort for 15 seconds.

12883.details:
Split Jerk
4 sets x 3 reps @ 70-75% or RPE 6-7
12883.notes:
Focus for most athletes today will be on skill development since we have the increased challenge of the footwork. The split jerk can allow us to move more load overhead due to the ability to get lower underneath the barbell and not have to elevate it as high. That said, newer athletes might find this variation more difficult while working out the timing, accuracy, coordination, and balance of the skill!
Regardless of your experience level, work at loads that allow you to build confidence through repetition. We’re aiming for crisp reps: powerful leg drive, clear timing, accurate footwork, and no press-outs! We will increase loading over the following three weeks.

12883.details:
AMRAP 12 MIN
200m Run
60 Double Unders
6 Wall Walks
12883.notes:
Intent: 3-4+ Rounds
Scale one, two, or all three movements so no individual round takes you longer than 4 minutes.
DU: < 1 min/round
A. 20-40 Double Unders
B. 45 sec DU Practice
C. 100 Single Unders
WW:
A. 2-4 Full ROM reps
B. 3 Partial ROM reps
C. 3 x 15 sec Angled Hollow Body Inversion Hold

12885.details:
A. Front Squat, 6 x 2 @ 80% – 85% / RPE 7-8
B. Deadlift, 5 x 3 @ RPE 7-8
C. Split Jerk, 4 x 3 @ 70-75% or RPE 6-7
D. Tempo Matador Dips, 4 x 6-10 @ 30×1
12885.notes:
Tomorrow we have power snatches, running, and power clean and jerks!
You may superset your main lift with another DB/KB or bodyweight movement.
Dips: If 10 reps at bodyweight on the tempo is no issue, add load. If needed, use a band or foot assistance that allows for at least 6 reps at a time, again maintaining tempo.

12885.details:
10 Rounds for time (5ea):
9 Strict Toes to Bars
9 Sandbag Squats
12885.notes:
Alternate complete rounds with your partner until each person has performed 5 rounds for a total of 10 as a team.
TTB: Control your tempo on the descent and keep your elbows and knees as straight as you can. Modify by bending the knees, moving through less ROM, or performing incline TTB.
SB: Choose a heavy bag you can complete 9 unbroken reps with!

12887.details:
For Time
“Isabel” 30 Power Snatches (135/95#)
1 Mile Run
“Grace” 30 Power Clean and Jerks
12887.notes:
Intent: 20-26 min
This workout combines two iconic benchmarks, Isabel and Grace, with a mile run in the middle… it’s meant to feel tough! The challenge is real, but keep breathing, stay composed, and chip away until the last rep.
Focusing on technique early on will allow you to keep working at higher intensity later: use the hook grip, feel your weight in the middle of your foot, keep the bar close, and maximize leg/hip drive on each rep of the barbell movements.
Snatches: Power. Settle into quick singles or small sets. Don’t waste energy chasing big unbroken sets.
Run: Here is where you regroup! Find a strong but steady pace. You should finish knowing you can get back on the barbell without crashing.
Clean and Jerks: Power. May feel heavy after the run, so stay calm, reset your grip each rep, and keep moving steadily.
Scaling Ideas
Weight:
135/115/95/75/65/45…
Volume:
20 Power Snatches
800m run
20 Clean and Jerks

12888.details:
A. Front Squat, 6 x 2 @ 80% – 85% / RPE 7-8
B. Deadlift, 5 x 3 @ RPE 7-8
C. Split Jerk, 4 x 3 @ 70-75% or RPE 6-7
D. Tempo Matador Dips, 4 x 6-10 @ 30×1
12888.notes:
Tomorrow we have front squats, running, chest to bar pull-ups, and overhead squats.
You may superset your main lift with another DB/KB or bodyweight movement.
Dips: If 10 reps at bodyweight on the tempo is no issue, add load. If needed, use a band or foot assistance that allows for at least 6 reps at a time, again maintaining tempo.

12888.details:
For Time
15-12-9 Calorie Row
9-12-15 Burpees over the Erg
12888.notes:
We did this workout on August 9, 2024.
If you can very comfortably row 20 calories in 1 minute, scale up the row calories to: 21-15-9. Burpee rep scheme remains the same (9-12-15).
Intent is < 6:00. This one is quick and dirty, and provides a perfect opportunity to push yourself. Scale as needed to achieve a high intensity effort from start to finish!
Scale A
12-10-8 Calorie Row
8-10-12 Burpees over the Rower
Scale B
12-10-8 Calorie Row
8-10-12 Burpees

12889.notes:
We have heavy triples today. Focus on bracing, maintaining tension at the bottom of the lift, and creating bar speed. Every rep should have a controlled and deliberate descent. Take time between reps at the top to reset; don’t rush.
Expect the weight to feel heavy but doable; leave just about 1 rep in the tank.
Rest 3 minutes or more between sets to recover fully.

12889.details:
For Time
130m Run
15 Overhead Squats (135/95/65#)
15 Chest to Bar Pull-Ups
270m Run
12 Overhead Squats
12 Chest to Bar Pull-Ups
400m Run
9 Overhead Squats
9 Chest to Bar Pull-Ups
12889.notes:
Intent ~8-12 min
Run Scaling: 130m>200>270m
OHS: Moderately heavy load that challenges your stability under fatigue. Reduce load as much as needed to achieve your best mechanics and range of motion today. An empty training bar will still provide a potent workout if the correct intent is applied!
Athletes may complete a full snatch that passes through a below-parallel squat as their first rep or use any method of power snatch to get the barbell overhead and then continue into their set.
CTB: For each rep to count, the athlete’s chest somewhere below the collarbone makes contact with the bar.
A. 12-9-6 CTB Kipping
B. 15-12-9 Chin Over Bar Kipping
C. 8-6-4 Strict Variation (CTB, chin over bar, foot assisted)

12890.details:
4 Intervals of:
In 3:00:
Bench Press x 15 Reps
AMRAP Row for Meters
Rest 3:00
12890.notes:
This is a repeat! Refer back to 11/16/2024.
This workout is 4 intervals of 3:00 on, 3:00 off with your score being weight used and total meters rowed.
Push hard on the row, but pace strategically so you don’t crash early.
Use the full 3:00 rest to recover; each interval should be treated like a fresh effort.
Bench Press: Try to use the same weight for all 4 sets on the bench press. Choose a weight that you can complete each round in 1–3 sets, about 65–70% of max. Loading at body weight or 3/4 bodyweight would be a lovely challenge for those capable.

12892.details:
A1. 4×6 Barbell Good mornings
A2. 4x6ea DB Reverse Lunges
12892.notes:
Today’s focus is posterior chain and single-leg strength. After a warm up set or two on the barbell, complete 4 sets of each as a superset. Rest about 60-90 seconds between A1 and A2, and about 1:30-2:00 between full rounds.
Good Mornings: Aim to go heavier than week 2, but only if you can keep a rigid, braced trunk, extended back, and controlled hip hinge.
DB Reverse Lunges: Suitcase style. Go heavier than week 1. Keep balance and smooth control through full range of motion, with the back knee touching the floor lightly on each rep.

12892.details:
6 Rounds For Time
12 KB Swings (70/53#)
12 Box Jump Overs
12892.notes:
This is a short, powerful workout! Push the pace but keep form sharp and make sure you’re organized for each box jump.
KB Swings: Aim for unbroken sets of 12 with a heavy bell. Drive through the hips, keep shoulders back, and let the bell float.
BJO: Two foot take off, then athletes must step down to the other side of the box. You may face one side of the box or position yourself horizontally to it, and you must travel over to the opposite side. Scale by reducing height of the box. Modify if needed by stepping up to and over the box with both feet.
Move steadily, minimize rest, and keep transitions quick.

12895.notes:
Today’s focus is on speed, accuracy, and confidence in the split jerk!
At 75–80%, the load should feel challenging but give you room to practice good mechanics.
Prioritize a smooth and controlled dip and fast drive, then punch yourself under the bar with strong, locked-out arms.
Hold your split stance for a moment before recovering, front foot back halfway, then back foot forward to meet it.
Every rep should look the same. Think about building consistency under load, not testing max strength.

12895.details:
18 Min for Quality
1:00 Bike for Calories @ RPE 5-6
80′ ea arm Single Arm Farmer Carry
130m Run @ RPE 5-6
80′ ea arm Single Arm Overhead Carry
12895.notes:
While this is assistance work, aim for minimal rest and try to just keep moving at a steady groove for the full time.
Bike and run at moderate efforts; you should be able to answer a question but not hold an entire long-winded conversation 😉 Set a baseline for calories in the first round and then aim to hit about that same number in your minute each time.
Choose moderate to heavy loading for the carries, as your mobility and stability allow. In the overhead position, reach through your shoulder and keep the elbow locked out the entire time.

12897.details:
A. Front Squat 4×3 @ 85% – 88% / RPE 8-9
B. Bench Press 4 sets x 10-15 reps
C. Deadlift, 4×5 @ RPE 7-7.5
D. Split Jerk, 4 sets x 2-3 reps @ 75-80% / RPE 7-8
12897.notes:
Tomorrow we have rowing, double unders and burpees.
You may superset your main lift with another DB/KB or bodyweight movement.
Deadlift: This is the same rep scheme as week 3 if you came to that class try to work a little bit heavier than that day.
Split Jerk: If you are new to this lift, keep a moderate load that allows you to focus on a solid footwork and speed. Mechanics first, then consistency then intensity!

12897.details:
AMRAP 8 MIN
4 Strict Chin Ups
8 Goblet Squats (32/24kg)
12 AbMat Sit-Ups
12897.notes:
Intent 4+ Rounds
Short and simple burner, aim for steady, unbroken rounds throughout the 8 minutes.
Chin ups: Strict and controlled; break early if needed to avoid hitting failure. Scale volume so you can complete the reps in under 30 sec per round or scale to foot-assisted reps.
Goblet squats: Should feel strong and smooth, keep the chest tall and heels down.
ABmat sit ups: Move fast through these ones but keep tension in the midline to protect your lower back.
The goal is constant movement, find a pace that lets you keep working without long breaks.

12899.details:
For Time:
Row 200 Calories
*After every 10 calories, one partner will perform 20 Double Unders and the other will perform 10 Burpees
12899.notes:
Intent: 24-30 minutes
One person rows at a time, with the following sequence:
A Rows 10 Calories (B is resting), then
*A performs 20 Double Unders, B performs 10 Burpees
B Rows 10 Calories (A is resting), then
*B performs 20 Double Unders, A performs 10 Burpees
Continue alternating with this format until a total of 200 calories have been rowed as a team!
