Ideally, each partner will end up completing 100 calories on the erg, 200 double unders, and 100 burpees.
Stay sharp on transitions, quick switches keep the pace high and prevent wasted time.
This workout is more about steady grind than sprinting; pace your burpees and double unders so you can maintain rhythm all the way through.
Scaling
Burpees: Reduce to 7–8 reps or no push up burpees.
Double Unders: 40 single unders or :20/:30 sec of DU’S attempts.
Row: Reduce total to 150 calories for newer athletes.

12901.details:
A. Front Squat 4×3 @ 85% – 88% / RPE 8-9
B. Bench Press 4 sets x 10-15 reps
C. Deadlift, 4×5 @ RPE 7-7.5
D. Split Jerk, 4 sets x 2-3 reps @ 75-80% / RPE 7-8
12901.notes:
Tomorrow we have front squats, power cleans, and running.
You may superset your main lift with another DB/KB or bodyweight movement.
Deadlift: This is the same rep scheme as week 3. If you came to that class try to work a little bit heavier than that day.
Split Jerk: If you are new to this lift, keep a moderate load that allows you to focus on a solid footwork and speed. Mechanics first, then consistency then intensity!

12901.details:
20 Rounds for Time
10 Ball Slams
100′ Sled Sprint
12901.notes:
In teams of four athletes, with one person working at a time, take turns on full rounds of the couplet until the team has finished 20 rounds, 5 for each person.
Use light weights today. Almost all athletes will get the most effective workout today by using an empty sled. Practice cycling your ball slams efficiently and then… sprint!

12904.notes:
Heavy doubles today.
Every rep should be controlled, tight, and explosive out of the hole.
Expect the bar to feel challenging and slower than previous weeks, but form must stay sharp. Leave about 1 rep in the tank.
Rest ~3 minutes between sets to recover fully and keep quality high.

12904.details:
3 Rounds for Time:
550m Run
7 Power Cleans 185/135#
Intent <15 min
12904.notes:
This workout is meant to be a gritty, medium length effort with a balance of running and heavy barbell work.
The 550m run should feel like ~2:30–3:00 of work at a steady but pushable pace. Use it as controlled effort, not a jog.
The 7 power cleans should be heavy enough that you need to break into singles or small sets. Move efficiently, set up well each rep, keep the bar close, and receive in a strong, stable position.
Aim for consistent round times and avoid blowing up early.
Scaling
Weight: 155/135/115/95/65 Reduce load to allow steady singles with good form and/or cap barbell reps at 5.
Run: 400m/270m

12906.notes:
Spend time dialing in the swing and timing, strong, controlled kip with active lats and tight body line.
Don’t rush the turnover; wait until you feel your hips rise before pulling the bar down and behind you.
Keep your arms straight longer and use your hips to create lift, not just your arms.
Some helpful cues:
“Push down on the bar, not away.”
“Hips to bar, then pull through.”
Scaling
Work on kip swings, chest-to-bar pull-ups, jumping bar muscle-ups, or transition drills using a low bar setup or band.

12906.details:
4 Rounds, Each for Time
15/12 Bike Calories
5 Bar Muscle-ups
*Complete 1 round every 4 minutes. Go as fast as possible on each round.
12906.notes:
Straightforward intervals today, so choose a gymnastic scale that challenges your skill and strength. You should aim to work hard for all 4 rounds and choose a variation that allows you to be successful, rather than hit a wall of failing multiple reps or sacrificing range of motion.
Bike < 90 sec. Scale back as needed.
BMU Scaling
A. 2-4 reps
B. 10 CTB Pull-Ups + 10 Strict Dips (matador/ring)
C. 10 Kipping Pull-Ups + 10 Box Dips
D. 5 Strict Pull-Ups (bw or assisted) + 10 Box Dips

12907.details:
A1. 4×6 Barbell Romanian Deadlifts @ 3111
A2. 4x6ea DB Bulgarian Split Squats
12907.notes:
Posterior chain strength and balance! Move with control and tension. After 2-3 warm up sets on the barbell, perform the two movements as a superset, resting about 60-90 sec between each. You should leave a little in the tank (RPE 7–8). Each set should feel challenging but not grindy.
RDLs: Aim to go heavier than Weeks 1 and 4. Hinge at the hips with a flat back, soft knees, and full hamstring stretch each rep. If you’re very mobile and stable, try adding a deficit by standing on a plate for extra range.
Bulgarian split squats: Should be steady and balanced, keep your chest tall, front foot flat, and knee tracking over toes.
Tempo and control are key! Think strength through tension, not speed.

12907.details:
18 min for Quality:
1:00 Sandbag Carry
30-45 sec each Stagger Stance Wall Sit Hold
1:00 Bike/Row/Jog
20 Tuck Ups
12907.notes:
This is a 18-minute quality-focused piece, aim for steady effort and control rather than intensity.
Sandbag Carry: Stay tall, brace your core, and keep steady breathing, switch positions if needed (bear hug, shoulder).
Stagger stance wall sit: Should challenge your quads. Keep your back flat to the wall.
Bike/row/jog: Active recovery. Keep it light and rhythmic to bring your heart rate down.
Tuck Ups: Tight core, controlled reps, and focus on hollow body tension.
Scaling
Wall Sit: Two legs
Tuck ups: For folks struggling to coordinate upper/lower body timing and reseting to a strong hollow body shape after each rep, do knee tucks!

12911.notes:
Today’s goal is still speed, accuracy, and confidence under the bar, not maximal load. The weight should feel challenging but allow for crisp, consistent reps. Every rep should look the same!
Focus on an upright dip, explosive drive, and fast punch under the bar. Land in a stable split stance, front foot flat, front shin vertical, back heel lifted, knees bent, and bar stacked directly over the shoulders.
Hold your catch position for a brief pause before recovering, front foot back, then back foot forward.

12911.details:
3 Rounds for Total Reps
1:00 Wall Walks
1:00 Shuttle Run (40 ft)
1:00 Alternating DB Snatch (50/35/20#)
1:00 Bike
1:00 Rest
12911.notes:
This is a Fight Gone Bad-style workout. Athletes will start at various stations. On a running clock, accumulate reps at each station. There is no extra rest or transition time between stations. Everyone will move through a 4 minute round and rest at the same time on the fifth minute in each round.
This workout is all about steady, sustained effort across movements. Pace early and aim to stay consistent through all 3 rounds to get the most work done in the total time allotted.
Wall walks: Move smoothly and avoid rushing; focus on strong shoulders and controlled descents. Scale range of motion or accumulate time in an angled hollow inversion hold.
Shuttle run: 1 rep = 40 feet = 20 ft down and 20 ft back.
DB snatches: Alternate arms each rep, keep the back flat, and use your hips to drive the dumbbell overhead.
Bike: Find a solid pace you can hold for the minute without redlining.
Use the 1-minute rest to walk around, shake out your arms, and control your breathing before the next round.

12913.details:
A. Front Squats 4×2 @ 88% – 90% / RPE 8-9
B. Weighted Chin-ups 3-3-3-3-3
C. Barbell Romanian Deadlifts 4×6 @ 3111 Tempo
D. Split Jerk, 4 sets x 2 reps @ 80%-85%+
12913.notes:
Tomorrow we have wall ball, double unders, and toes to bar.
You may superset your main lift with another DB/KB or bodyweight movement.
RDLs: This is the same rep scheme as weeks 1 and 4. If you hit those exposures, try to work a little bit heavier today while maintaining form and tempo.
Split Jerk: If you are new to this lift, keep a moderate load that allows you to focus on a solid footwork and speed. Mechanics first, then consistency then intensity!
Chin-Up Progression: We last saw weighted chin-ups (doubles) in Week 4, so you can track back for guidance today. Do a couple of warm up sets (foot assisted ring pull-ups, negatives, lock offs, etc.). Then choose a difficult variation for you that allows for consistent mechanics and full ranges of motion. Examples:
A. 5 Sets x 3 weighted Chin-Ups, building to find a heavy triple
B. 5-7 Sets x 1-3 bodyweight Chin-Ups or Negatives
C. 5 Sets x 5 tough reps of Box Pike or Foot Assisted Chin-Ups

12913.details:
AMRAP 12 MIN
Row for Meters
*Non-rowing partner holds a Forearm Plank. Trade off as desired.
12913.notes:
Team effort today! Your meters only count when your partner is holding a solid forearm plank, so communication and timing are key.
Take turns rowing in consistent, powerful intervals (e.g., 250–500m), depending on your capacity and how long your partner can hold the plank.
Row: Stay strong and efficient, big drive with the legs, smooth pull, and controlled recovery.
Plank: Focus on tight glutes, braced core, and steady breathing. Avoid sagging hips or piking up.
The goal is steady output for 12 minutes, not an all-out sprint early. Find a rhythm that keeps both athletes moving and engaged.

12914.details:
For Time
60 Wall Ball Shots (20#, 10′ / 14#, 9′)
180 Double Unders
60 Toes to Bar
12914.notes:
This is a chipper style workout, where all repetitions of the first movement must be completed before moving to the second, and again to the third.
Create a gameplan today, don’t just go in blind. That being said, staying flexible with the plan will help many of us achieve our best time!
If you’re typically conservative, maybe today is a good opportunity to push for bigger sets. If you often overestimate your capacity and flame out early, perhaps playing with the other end of the spectrum is worth a try.
Either way… work hard and have fun with this one!
Wall Ball: 1-4 sets. Scale med ball weight and target height. further as needed.
Double Unders: Scale to a rep count you can complete in under 5 minutes.
TTB: 3-8 sets. Scale to 40 kipping reps, 30 strict reps, partial range of motion, or 60 sit-ups.

12916.details:
A. Front Squats 4×2 @ 88% – 90% / RPE 8-9
B. Weighted Chin-ups 3-3-3-3-3
C. Barbell Romanian Deadlifts 4×6 @ 3111 Tempo
D. Split Jerk, 4 sets x 2 reps @ 80%-85%+
12916.notes:
Tomorrow we have heavy front squats, KB swings, and push-ups.
You may superset your main lift with another DB/KB or bodyweight movement.
RDLs: This is the same rep scheme as weeks 1 and 4. If you hit those exposures, try to work a little bit heavier today while maintaining form and tempo.
Split Jerk: If you are new to this lift, keep a moderate load that allows you to focus on a solid footwork and speed. Mechanics first, then consistency then intensity!
Chin-Up Progression: We last saw weighted chin-ups (doubles) in Week 4, so you can track back for guidance today. Do a couple of warm up sets (foot assisted ring pull-ups, negatives, lock offs, etc.). Then choose a difficult variation for you that allows for consistent mechanics and full ranges of motion. Examples:
A. 5 Sets x 3 weighted Chin-Ups, building to find a heavy triple
B. 5-7 Sets x 1-3 bodyweight Chin-Ups or Negatives
C. 5 Sets x 5 tough reps of Box Pike or Foot Assisted Chin-Ups

12916.details:
For Time
270m Run, each
400m Run, each
550m Run, each
12916.notes:
Buddy up and get a move on! Partner A starts by running 270m, and upon returning to the gym tags in Partner B to do their length.
With about 3/4 mile total distance here, these should be tough efforts right out the gate.
The stronger runner (or whoever is more confident in “recovering” better) should likely go first today, as they’ll have less rest than the second partner going into each subsequently longer interval.
Scale: If your mile pace is over 12 min or you are building your tolerance to running, consider scaling to:
200m / 270m / 400m (Total distance is just over half a mile)

12919.notes:
Today is a heavy front squat day! Focus on tension, control, and confidence under load.
At 90–95% / RPE 8.5–9, every single should feel heavy but technically solid. Take time to brace properly. Big breath, tight core, elbows high, and chest tall. Keep your midline engaged throughout the rep, especially in the turnover, and drive straight up out of the hole.
Treat each single as practice for your next PR: perfect setup, perfect execution!
Rest 2–3 minutes between sets to recover and maintain quality.

This short AMRAP is a grip and upper-body endurance burner. Pace early and stay smooth.
The rep scheme climbs fast, so don’t sprint the early rounds; find a rhythm you can sustain. The goal is steady movement for the full 8 minutes; avoid long rests once fatigue sets in.
For KB swings, keep the hinge sharp, drive with your hips, not your arms. Stay tall and breathe at the top.
Push-ups will add up quickly! Maintain tight midline, full range of motion, and break before hitting failure.
PU Scale:
A. Volume (ex: 3-6-9-12-etc.)
B. Incline Push-up — choose a height you can complete about 8-12 unbroken reps at when fresh!

12920.notes: Your coach will take you through a short progression to work on the footwork and foundations of this skill. Beginner athletes can expect to get an understanding of mechanics needed and elements to work on. More experienced athletes should come ready to learn how to make their existing skills more efficient!

12920.details:
20 Minutes for Quality
1-3 Rope Climbs (15′)
30 sec each: DB Side Plank
400m Run
12920.notes:
The intent for today is sustainable, quality effort. Choose a rope climb scale that allows you to practice the skill while working safely under moderate fatigue. If you’re advanced, you might see how quickly you can complete 3 reps each time you get back to the rope.
*If you missed yesterday’s workout, option is to sub in 10-20 push-ups per round instead of side planks!
A. 1 Partial Height Climb
B. 3-5 Rig Pull-Up with Rope Footwork
C. 2-3 Supine-to-Stand-to-Supine Climbs

12920.details:
2 Sets
10-15+ DB Supinated Bicep Curls
10-15 Banded Reverse Flyes
12920.notes:
Curls: Pick a weight you cannot complete more than 20 reps with when fresh. On your second set through, go to failure. Resist the urge to use momentum.
Flyes: Keep your ribs stacked over your pelvis (not flared forward) and squeeze/wrap the shoulder-blades together as you pull back.

12921.details:
A1. Deadlift, 8-6-4-8
A2. Split Squat Pallof Hold, 4 x 20 sec each
12921.notes:
Deadlift: Today’s sets are a “wave.” Begin with 2-4 warm-up sets to find a starting point for your first work set: a moderately heavy 8 reps. Increase the weight for the set of 6 and again for the set of 4 reps.
The final 8 reps will be a “drop set.” You can repeat the same load you used in the first set or ideally go a bit heavier.
SSPH: Hover the back knee just a couple inches off of the floor throughout the hold. Keep ribcage stacked over the pelvis and torso upright.

12921.details:
Tabata Mash-Ups!
8 Rounds / 4 Minutes
A. Double Unders
B. Sandbag Bearhug Hold
Rest 2 min
8 Rounds / 4 Minutes
A. Box Jumps (24/20″)
B. Dual KB Suitcase Hold (32/24kg ea)
12921.notes:
Tabata is 20 seconds of work / 10 seconds of rest. Alternate movements back and forth (A/B) for 8 total rounds, 4 of each. Rest and use the same structure for the second couplet.
Go for max reps each round on the jumping movements and choose challenging weights for your holds. Grit it out!
Use this format to practice double unders, regardless of skill level.
Land as tall and lightly on the box as possible today. Fully extend the knees and hips before stepping down.

12923.notes: After a few minutes to warm up, perform a set of 2 jerks every 2:00 for 5 sets. If technique is on point and reps are feeling crisp, aim to go a bit heavier than last week (80-85%). If not or if you’re newer to this variation, stay at a load that allows you to make adjustments and practice good reps to finish out this cycle!

12923.details:
For Time:
1000/800m Row
– into –
10 Dual DB Devil’s Press
20 Dual DB Front Rack Lunges
30 Burpees
20 Dual DB Front Rack Lunges
10 Dual DB Devil’s Press
12923.notes:
Workout courtesy of Coach Phil!
Time Cap: 15 min
Row < 4 min
DB: 50/35/20# ea hand.
Choose a DB weight that you can maintain proper midline stabilization with and good overhed position at the top of each rep of the devil’s press, as well as complete the lunges in 1-2 sets.
This is a challenging movement to organize, especially under fatigue. Remove ego and scale as needed!

12924.details:
18 Min for Quality
16 Alternating Tall Kneeling Rotational Ball Slams
30 sec each Single Leg Hamstring Bridge Hold
1:00 Bike/Row/Jog/Jump Rope
30 sec L-Sit
12924.notes:
Today is about control, position, and quality movement, not intensity or speed. Move with purpose and stay focused on good mechanics!
Ball Slams: Rotate through the torso, stay tall, and use your hips/core to generate power rather than just throwing with the arms.
Single-leg hamstring hold: Drive your heel down, keep your hips level, and focus on feeling the hamstring load, not your lower back!
Cardio: Should be smooth, conversational, and used as active recovery before the core work.
L-sit: Stay tight and fight for a strong position; break once or twice if needed, but maintain quality throughout. Scale to a tuck hold or floor pike hold.

12924.details:
A. Front Squats 5X1 @ 90% – 95% / RPE 8.5-9
B. Deadlift 8-6-4-8
C. Split Jerk 5×2, building
D. Tempo Matador Dips, 4 x 6-8 @ 30×1
12924.notes:
Tomorrow we have air squats, power cleans, strict pull-ups, and running.
You may superset your main lift with another DB/KB or bodyweight movement.
Front Squat: Heavy singles mean strong bracing, tall chest, and confidence out of the bottom.
Deadlifts: The 8-6-4-8 wave should build, then back off. Keep your back tight and hinge clean.
Split Jerk: If you are new to this lift, keep a moderate load that allows you to focus on a solid footwork and speed. Mechanics first, then consistency then intensity!
Matador Dips: Time under tension, stay strict, feel the tempo; and build control in the pressing muscles.

12925.details:
6 Rounds for Time
30 Air Squats
19 Power Cleans (135/95#)
7 Strict Pull-ups
400m Run
12925.notes:
Today is the final Saturday of our 8-week cycle, and we’re closing it out with purpose. “Hotshots 19” is a tribute workout honoring the 19 members of the Granite Mountain Hotshots firefighting team who tragically lost their lives while fighting a fire in Yarnell, Arizona.
Approach this piece with respect, grit, and intention. This is a long workout, so settle into a steady rhythm.
Air Squat: Move with quality and keep the integrity of the range of motion!
Power Cleans: Stay disciplined with controlled singles or small sets.
Strict pull-ups: Break early if you need to, to keep form sharp.
Run: Use it to breathe, reset, and stay mentally locked in, preparing to come back in and work with focus, toughness, and consistency, round after round.
You’ve built strength and capacity these past 8 weeks and the whole year! Today is where it shows.
Scaling
This Hero WOD is long and high volume. Reduce the reps and load to keep this workout under 40 minutes.
Power Clean: 135/115/95/75/55
Pull-Ups: Strict, Assisted, Kipping, Ring Rows
Run: Suggest keeping the full volume run today OR complete 200m run + 400m bike per round
Newer or deconditioned athletes might also consider scaling their version of the workout to 4 rounds instead of 6 so there is less overall volume of work today.

12926.details:
A. Front Squats 5X1 @ 90% – 95% / RPE 8.5-9
B. Deadlift 8-6-4-8
C. Split Jerk 5×2, building
D. Tempo Matador Dips, 4 x 6-8 @ 30×1
Front Squat: Heavy singles mean strong bracing, tall chest, and confidence out of the bottom.
Deadlifts: The 8-6-4-8 wave should build, then back off. Keep your back tight and hinge clean.
Split Jerk: If you are new to this lift, keep a moderate load that allows you to focus on a solid footwork and speed. Mechanics first, then consistency then intensity!
Matador Dips: Time under tension, stay strict, feel the tempo; and build control in the pressing muscles.

12926.notes:
Partners alternate full rounds. Partner A completes 20 sit-ups + 12/9 bike, then Partner B does the same.
Score = total rounds.
Sustainable, aerobic pacing. Rounds should take ~1:10–1:40, depending on bike power. Goal is to maintain relatively consistent round times across all 15 minutes, not fade in the back half.
Sit-ups: Smooth and unbroken. Use them to breathe before the bike.
Bike: < 45 sec at a strong effort, controlled push. Beware of going all-out, especially in the initial rounds.
Focus on quick transitions on and off the bike. Communicate with your partner, call out when you’re a few cals from done so they can get ready.

12930.details:
A: Pull-Ups
4×5-8 reps
B: DB Curls
3×10-15 reps
12930.notes:
Pull-ups: Perform 3–4 warm-up sets with ring rows, scap pulls, and light assisted pull-ups, then complete 4 sets of 5-8 reps. Choose the hardest variation you can perform with full range of motion — bodyweight, weighted, or self-assisted. Cluster sets (e.g., 3 reps + 2 reps) are allowed if you can’t perform 5-8 unbroken BW reps but have strict pull-ups. Leave 0–1 reps in reserve.
Curls: perform 1 quick warm-up set followed by two sets in the 10-15 range which should both go to or near failure.

12930.details:
AMRAP 12:00
12 Calorie Row or 9 Calorie Bike
9 Burpees
6 Dumbbell Thrusters (50/35/20)
12930.notes: This should be a fast-moving triplet. Go heavy but unbroken on the thrusters and be consistent with the bike/rows aiming for around :45-1:00 efforts. Goal is 4–5+ rounds.

12932.details:
A1: Bench Press 3×10–12
A2: Bent over DB Rows 3×8–12
12932.notes:
Bench Press: Perform 3-4 warm-up sets, then work up through three progressive heavy sets in the 10-12 range.
Rows: Hinge over and use two DB’s at the same time. Perform 1-2 warm-up sets then 3 progressive weight sets going near or to failure.

12932.details:
21–15–9 reps for time of:
Deadlifts (+/185/135/95)
Matador Dips
12932.notes:
This should be a lighter and faster version of “Elizabeth”. Aim to go unbroken or in as few sets as possible while maintaining good form and range of motion.That being said, your dips should maintain a controlled tempo and full rom. If you can do 225/155 deadlifts unbroken, scale up.
Dip scaling Options:
(+) Ring Dips (21-15-9 or 15-9-6)
Matador Dips (21-15-9 or 15-9-6)
Banded Matador Dips
Bench Dips

12935.notes: Perform 3–4 progressive warm-up sets then complete 3 progressive and challenging sets of 10-12 reps. Rest 3-5 minutes between sets. Leave 2–3 reps in reserve each set. Weights should feel tough but doable.

12935.details:
8 Rounds for time of:
12 Strict Toes to Bars
16 DB Suitcase Walking Lunges
12935.notes:
Partners alternate complete rounds until each person has completed 4. This workout should take somewhere between 10 and 12 minutes for most teams and is very grippy!
Lunges: Heavy and unbroken +/50s/35s/25s/-
T2Bs: 1-4 Sets (this will add up!)
T2B Scaling Options
Strict T2B 12/8 reps
12 Partial ROM or Leg Raises
16 Sit-Ups or Tuck-Ups

12936.details:
Every 2:00 x 3 Sets Perform
3 Power Cleans
Every 3:00 x 3 Sets Perform
2 Power Cleans
Every 3:00 x 3 Sets Perform
1 Power Clean
12936.notes:
In this workout you’ll perform 9 total sets by way of 3×3, 3×2 and 3×1 power cleans on a clock. Try to add a little weight every set as long as your technique is crisp. If you’re not at a point where you feel confident going very heavy you can keep the reps at 2s or 3s and work a little more volume. No touch and go reps today, focus on a proper set up every lift.
ex: 135×3, 155×3, 175×3, 185×2, 195×2, 205×2, 215×1, 220×1, 225×1

12936.details:
For Time:
21 Kettlebell Swings
63 Double Unders
15 Kettlebell Swings
45 Double Unders
9 Kettlebell Swings
27 Double Unders
12936.notes:
This should fast (3-4 minutes) and attempted unbroken. Get out of your comfort zone on the Kettlebell weight today and keep it in 5th gear.
KB: +/32kg/24kg/20kg/-
Double Under Scaling
A: 63-45-27
B 42-30-18
C: 21-15-9
D: Heavy Rope 30-20-10

12939.details: Anyone who wears a costume today gets something free out of the fridge!

Bench Press 3×10-12
Dent Over DB Rows 3×8-12
Back Squat 3×10-12
Power Cleans, 3-3-3-3-3
Shoulder Press 12-12-12
12939.notes:
Perform 3–4 progressive warm-up sets for your chosen lift(s).
Work within the prescribed rep ranges, leaving 1–2 reps in reserve.

12939.details:
AMRAP 13:00
13 Kipping Pull-Ups
13 Burpees
While one partner Air Bikes
12939.notes:
One partner starts on the pull-ups and burpees while the other starts on the air bike. Everytime one partner completes the 13 & 13 reps you switch. Score is total cals biked at the end of 13:00.
The pull-ups and burpees should take somewhere around 1:1:30 per round with each person doing 4-5 rounds of the couplet.
Kipping Pull-Ups
13/9 Kipping Pull-Ups
9/6 Strict
13 Ring Rows or Jumping

12941.details:
3 Rounds For Total Reps of:
1:00 Wall Ball Shots (20lbs/10′) (14lbs/9′)(10lbs/9′)
1:00 Alternating Dumbbell Snatch (50/35/20)
1:00 Box Jump Overs (24″/20″/Step Overs)
1:00 Shoulder to Overhead (95/65/45)
1:00 Row, calories
1:00 Rest
12941.notes: Perform 1 minute of work at each of the 5 stations, moving immediately to the next station after 1 minute. The clock does not reset or stop between exercises. A one-minute break is allowed before repeating each round. One point is given for each rep or calorie. Each team member will start at a different station and rest at the same time. Teams with 6 members will have two people start on the same station, but they will use different equipment (e.g., separate barbells, med balls).

12942.details:
Pull-Ups 4×5
DB Curls 2×10-15
Bench Press 3×10-12
Dent Over DB Rows 3×8-12
Back Squat 10-12
Power Cleans, 3-3-3-3-3
Shoulder Press 12-12-12
12942.notes:
Perform 3–4 progressive warm-up sets for your chosen lift(s).
Work within the prescribed rep ranges, leaving 1–2 reps in reserve.

12942.details:
800m Burden Carry
Sandbag Carry
Kettlebell Farmer’s Carry
12942.notes:
2 Partners head out for the 800m with a sandbag and pair of kettlebells alternating the implements whenever they want — one athlete always carries the sandbag, the other always carries the kettlebells.
Switch often to keep moving; goal is continuous forward progress.
Sandbag should be heavy enough to require breaks but still allow 100–200 ft stretches. We encourage you to bear hug the sandbag, only shouldering it if you can no longer bear hug it. Kettlebells should challenge grip and posture

12944.details:
A1: Chin-Ups
4×5–8 reps
A2: 1:00 Partner Sorenson Holds x4 Sets
12944.notes:
Chin-Ups: Perform 3–4 warm-up sets (ring rows, banded chin-ups, or assisted variations). Then complete 4 working sets of 6–8 reps. Choose the hardest variation you can perform with full range of motion — weighted, bodyweight, or assisted. Leave 0–1 reps in reserve. Cluster sets (e.g., 3 reps + 2 reps) are allowed if you can’t perform 5-8 unbroken BW reps.
After your warm-ups, start supersetting the partner sorenson holds.

12944.details:
Every 4:00 x 4 Rounds:
400 Run
15 Kipping Toes to Bars
12944.notes:
Every 4 minutes head out on the run + kipping toes to bars. Each interval should take 2:45-3:30. Scale the run distance or T2B volume if needed. If you fall behind the clock, scale the volume or finish the remaining volume for time.
Kipping Toes to Bars
15/9/6 Reps
15/9 Hanging Leg Raises
15 Sit-Ups

12945.notes: Perform 3-4+ warm-up sets, then work up through three progressive heavy sets in the 8-10 range. Leave 0-2 reps in reserve.

12945.details:
4 Progressive Sets of:
8-12 Pendlay Rows
8-12 Barbell Roll outs
~2:00 Air bike recovery
12945.notes: Work up through 4 progressive sets on the couplet, rest roughly 2:00 on the air bike. If you’re not coming tomorrow, consider performing 8-12 Goblet Squats instead while your partner works the couplet.

12947.notes: Perform 3–4 progressive warm-up sets then complete 3 progressive and challenging sets of 6-8 reps. Rest 3-4 minutes between sets. Leave 1–2 reps in reserve each set.

12947.details:
5 Rounds for time of:
24 Calorie Row
24 WTD Step-Overs
12947.notes:
In this 12-16′ workout partners work together to divide and complete the reps per movement until 5 rounds have been completed. So partner A completes 12 cals on the rower, then partner B completes 12 cals etc.
Row
Each 24 cal row should not take more than 2:00 to complete, scale down to 10 or 8 cals per person if needed.
Step-Overs
(50s/35s/20s)
These Step overs are full extension on top of the box. Sorry not sorry. Load with two Dumbbells held at the hang.

12950.details:
Every 3:00 for 9 Sets Perform:
65 Double Unders
3 Power Snatches
12950.notes:
Compare to 11.14.24
Each interval should take you no longer than 1:30 to complete .
Jump Rope
The 65 Doubles should be performed in 1:00 or less. If you can’t, do AMRAP double or single unders (or heavy rope singles) to the :50 mark each round then transition to the power snatches.
Power Snatches
There are 27 total reps in this workout with significant time between sets. These should be performed as singles dropped from the top, if you can cycle them it’s too light. Each rep should be consistent and crisp.
If you’re new to snatching, you could also perform 5 hang power snatches each round instead.

12951.details:
Chin-Ups 4×5–8 reps
Cluster 1-1-1-1-1
Bench Press 4×8-10 reps
Front Squat 4×6-8 reps
Power Snatch 3-3-3-3-3
12951.notes: Perform 3–4 progressive warm-up sets for your chosen lift(s). Work within the prescribed rep ranges, leaving 1–2 reps in reserve.

12951.details:
In 5:00
15-9-6
Burpees
Kettlebell Swings
In remaining time, AMRAP bike cals.
12951.notes: The couplet should be heavy, unbroken and completed in around 3:00 give or take. Once you get on the bike, power through the remaining time!

12953.details:
5 Rounds for time of:
Run 400m
8 Clusters (+/155/135/95/75/-)
12 Kipping Pull-Ups
12953.notes:
This workout will take most people around 18-22 minutes. Stay consistent on your runs and go heavy enough on the clusters that the weight slows you down to steady singles.
Kipping Pull-Ups
(+) 4-8 Bar Muscle-Ups
(+) 12 Chest to Bar
12/8 Kipping
8-6 Strict or Banded
12 Jumping

12954.details:
Chin-Ups 4×5–8 reps
Cluster 1-1-1-1-1
Bench Press 4×8-10 reps
Front Squat 4×6-8 reps
Power Snatch 3-3-3-3-3
12954.notes: Perform 3–4 progressive warm-up sets for your chosen lift(s). Work within the prescribed rep ranges, leaving 1–2 reps in reserve.

12954.details:
4 Progressive Sets of:
8-16 Matador Dips
8-16 Anchored Weighted Sit-Ups
3 High Box Jumps
12954.notes: Work through 4 progressive sets of the triplet and aim to finish in under 20 minutes. The matadors may be weighted, BW banded or bench Dips can be substituted. The box jumps can be as high as you’re brave enough to try, we’ll be using soft boxes for some of the higher attempts!

12956.details:
2-2-1-1-1 Reps for max load of:
Hand over hand rope pull
Sled Push back
12956.notes:
Pull the sled hand over hand then push it back to the start, perform two sets of 2 reps then three to four singles trying to add weight each set.
The load should never be so heavy that it stops moving during your pull or push, but go for it.

12956.details:
10 Rounds for time of:
3/2 Wall Walks
16 DB Deadlifts
12956.notes:
Partners alternate complete rounds until each person has completed 5. This workout should be around 10-13 minutes with each round taking about 1-1:20. Scale volume on wall walks to 2 reps or cap it at 8 rounds.
Deadlift +/50s/35s/20s/-

12957.notes: After 4-5 warm-ups build to a heavy 5-8 over 3 work sets. Leave 0-2 reps in reserve.

12957.details:
For Time:
30/24 Calorie Row
15 Burpees
30 Wall Ball Shots
15 Burpees
30/24 Calorie Row
12957.notes: The Row should be around or under 2:00. If you’re going over 2:30 on the row scale to 24 cals. This workout will take most people around 6-9 minutes

12958.details:
4 Intervals of:
6 Weighted Chin-Ups (50/35/20)
24 Tuck-Ups
75 Double Unders
Rest as needed between rounds. Capped at 20:00
12958.notes:

Bike:
-Newer to rope climbs? Aim for RPE 5-7 on the bike to maximize your chance of being successful across all 5 rounds.
-More advanced climber? Push bike pace to RPE 7-8+.

The bar will come out of the rack today.
Build to your heaviest technically-sound triple in the split jerk within 20 minutes.

Quality over load! We want heavy weight, but only on reps you can catch cleanly overhead and hold with stability.

13020.notes:

Press straight up, finish with bicep by ear and ribs down.
No leaning, no knee dip, no “sneaky jerk.”
Sorenson hold: Neutral spine, think long, not arched.
Arms crossed or hands at temples.
Breathe behind the brace.
Add light plate hug if athlete is rock-solid and has time.
Pallof: Front heel down, back knee soft.
Hands extended straight out from chest.
Don’t let the band pull you off center, resist quietly.

13025.notes:
Time Cap: 32 minutes. This is the same workout we did last year — try to beat your score!
In round 1 perform 1 wall walk.
In round 2 perform 2 burpees and then 1 wall walk.
In round 3 perform 3 DB Thrusters, then 2 burpees, then 1 wall walk.
In round 4 perform 4 DB Push Press, 3 DB Thrusters, 2 burpees, 1 wall walk.
Continue in the same fashion, adding a new exercise each round.
As noted above, renegade rows are 6 total alternating, 3 each side, reverse lunges are 8 total, 4 each side, and snatches are 12 total alternating, 6 each side.
Scaling Ideas!
Pick a DB weight that you can use for all of the movements. A good challenge would be to see if you can do the rows, squats, push presses, and thrusters in an unbroken complex. If you have one movement that is a big limiting factor, then a second set of weights might be appropriate.
Wall Walk:
A. Partial range of motion
B. Angled hollow body inversion hold x 10 seconds
C. Box Piked Handstand Hold x 10 seconds
Knees to Elbows: Straight arms throughout. RX’d movement is the knees touching the elbow joint, not the triceps/upper arms. Scale to hanging knee raise with knees above hips.

13026.notes:
Move with intention, especially on the core pieces.
Use the cardio minute to reset breathing, not spike intensity.
Sled Push: Use a moderate, repeatable load. Maintain a tall, braced posture and steady steps. Movement should be smooth and continuous, not maximal.
L-Sit: Keep toes in line with or above hips. Scale to single knee bend OR both knees tucked.
Adductor Plank: Maintain stacked hips and a long spine. Scale by assisting with bottom leg OR bend the knees and place shin on the bench.

13026.notes:

Shuttle Run: 1 rep = 40′ = down and back across the far tape lines.
Choose a heavy bag for you and focus on efficiency:
-Set up: bag between feet (not in front)
-Hands scoop under bag
-Get low, get braced
-Lap it and bring feet under hips
-Drive through legs and hips
-Don’t pull from the arms or heave from the shoulders

Breathe steadily and aim for smooth, repeatable sets rather than sprinting early. Scale along the progression in this video if still working on positional strength and coordination!

13029.notes:
In a total of 6-8 sets, build to a heavy set of 3 with full control and no leg drive. Prioritize a strong setup with tight glutes, braced midline, and a vertical bar path. The final heavy set should be challenging and technically sound, not a grind with loss of position.
After your heavy triple, perform an AMRAP at 70% of that top set. Reps should be smooth and repeatable with consistent tempo. Stop the set when bar speed slows significantly or posture breaks down. Focus on quality pressing and shoulder stability rather than pushing to failure.
The press is typically the lightest of our “slow” barbell lifts (squat, deadlift, bench, press), so don’t be afraid to employ the fractional plates today!

13029.notes:
DB Reverse Flies: Light to moderate loads and move with control. Emphasize squeezing the shoulder blades together without shrugging or swinging the weights.
Bicep Curls: Choose a load that allows full range of motion and steady tempo. Keep elbows fixed and avoid using momentum to move the dumbbells.
HS Hold: Focus on stacked alignment with active shoulders and a braced midline. Break as needed to maintain quality. Scale to wall-facing holds, box pike holds, or shorter intervals if alignment cannot be maintained.

13031.details:
Pause Front Squat
3 x 5, building or across
*Pause for 2 secconds at bottom
13031.notes:
After 2-4 warm up sets, perform 3 work sets of 5 reps, either building in load across sets or holding the same weight for all sets. Pause for a full two seconds in the bottom while maintaining an upright torso, strong brace, and active elbows.
Prioritize position and control over load. The pause should be stable and balanced, not relaxed. Drive smoothly out of the bottom without bouncing or losing posture.

13031.details:
EMOM x 9 MIN
1. 40 sec Strict T2B/Knee Raises
2. 40 sec Hollow hold
3. 40 sec Sit ups
13031.notes:
Strict Toes-to-Bar/Knee Raises: Move with control and full tension. Avoid swinging and focus on pressing down through the bar while lifting with the core. Scale to partial ROM or knee raises or reduce time if strict form cannot be maintained.
Hollow Hold: Maintain a strong hollow position with lower back pressed into the floor and ribs down. Break early if tension is lost rather than letting the shape collapse.
Sit-Ups: Perform smooth, controlled reps with consistent breathing. Avoid rushing and use the remaining time to reset before the next minute.

13032.notes:
Whether or not you were lucky enough to hit this one in 2017 or 2021… let’s close out 2025 with it! 😈
This workout is a tough mental and physical grind. Top 5% athletes in the Open finished this under 14 minutes, with average times being much closer to the timecap. Commit to your effort for the long haul, work hard, and make yourself proud!
DB: 50/35/20# — Scale to a load you could do at least 10 unbroken reps with.
Box: 24/20″ — For further scaling, a step up and over the box is permitted with both feet touching the top.
Snatch: Rep is credited when knees, hips, and elbow of working arm are fully extended. The middle of the DB is in line with or behind the body when viewed from the side.
BBJO: Athlete faces the box, chest and thighs touching the ground at bottom of the burpee. Two foot take off to jump on the box. You may jump completely over the box, but feet must go over, not around. Rep is credited when both feet are on opposite side of the box.
If the BBJO is a particularly challenging movement for you, consider scaling to 10 or 12 reps per round, rather than 15. We encourage this scale before removing the push-up from the burpee.
